• "We must move faster," COP31 negotiations lead Australia says
  • COP31 goal: electrify more than a third of world economy by 2035
  • US shuns climate cooperation for second year in a row

Adds quote from Turkey President Erdogan in paragraph 10, replaces quote in final paragraph

By Simon Jessop and Tuvan Gumrukcu

ANTALYA, Turkey, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Leaders of the COP31 climate summit urged the world to accelerate the fight against global warming amid rising temperatures and worsening climate-driven disasters, as the annual meeting began in Turkey on Monday.

The comments at the start of the two-week UN conference were an appeal to governments to focus on climate, even as other international crises from war to soaring inflation and the uncertainty of artificial intelligence compete for their attention.

"The urgency of this moment must drive us forward," UN Climate Change Executive Secretary Simon Stiell said at the opening of the event on Turkey's Mediterranean coast, adding that progress so far was "nowhere near fast enough."

A report by the United Nations Environment Programme published in October said the world was already poised to overshoot 1.5 degrees Celsius of warming above pre-industrial times, the threshold set at the 2015 Paris climate summit to avoid the worst consequences of warming.

This year is on track to be one of the four hottest on record, driven by a powerful El Nino, a UN report showed on Monday.

It has also stood out with a series of extreme heatwaves across Western Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that triggered a catastrophic flood killing more than 1,450 people, with thousands still missing.

Turkey's COP31 presidency has focused this year's summit on a goal to electrify more than a third of the global economy by 2035, up from around a fifth today. It is asking nations to sign onto a pledge supporting that target.

Theoretically, such a goal could help reduce planet-warming emissions by speeding the global shift away from fossil fuel-powered vehicles, furnaces, boilers, cooking stoves, and other greenhouse gas-emitting equipment.

"We want people to feel the results of climate talks in daily life: in buildings that use less energy, in clean public transport, in energy they can afford and in new jobs," Turkey's COP31 President Murat Kurum said.

But climate advocates have criticised the pledge because it does not require the additional electricity to come from low-carbon sources, setting up an early fight over whether electrification alone should count as climate progress.

Turkish President Tayyip Erdogan said he hoped Turkey could deliver concrete results.

"Our goal is to make this summit a platform where concrete results are produced, where countries turn their pledges into action, because it is no longer time to make promises that remain on paper," Erdogan told reporters on a return flight from Azerbaijan, according to a transcript of his comments shared by his office on Monday.

WAR AND TECH

The Iran war has underscored the world's attachment to fossil fuels, as has Russia's invasion of Ukraine, though some say the wars have also shown the benefits of moving to renewables.

Now in its ninth month, the Iran war has severely disrupted Middle East oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz, lifting fuel prices around the globe and prompting a scramble for new supplies.

US President Donald Trump's administration — which is shunning climate talks for the second year running — has encouraged policies maximising oil, gas, and coal production to address the disruptions.

South Korea, India, Thailand and other Asian nations, meanwhile, have also increased their reliance on coal or taken steps to boost coal-fired power generation.

"A lot of people who previously might have been embarrassed to argue for continuing very high use of fossil fuel are now feeling empowered to make that case," said John Holdren of Harvard University, who was a science adviser to Barack Obama when he was US president.

At the same time, the deployment of renewable energy has also risen, driven by surging exports of cheap clean tech from China.

Stiell told the summit renewables were the clear answer to improving energy security.

"This year's fossil fuel cost chaos has delivered a global shockwave, hitting households hard and spreading inflation like a cancer," he said.

"But the solutions are clear," he added, saying renewable energy installations had already saved the global economy hundreds of billions of dollars.

The rapid rollout of AI is also complicating talks, driving a surge in global power demand and contributing to rising greenhouse gas emissions.

Turkey will call on governments, businesses and other institutions at COP31 to sign a pledge outlining principles to ensure AI is developed and deployed sustainably.

Chris Bowen, Australia's president of COP31 negotiations, said he hoped the conference would show the world that multilateralism works.

"Let's show future generations that this generation was equal to the moment, equal to the challenge," he said.

(Reporting by Ezgi Erkoyun, Tuvan Gumrukcu, Valerie Volcovici, Simon Jessop, and Sarah McFarlane; Writing by Richard Valdmanis; Editing by David Gregorio, Kate Mayberry and Jan Harvey)

Chile es el mayor productor global del metal rojo.

Description: Nvidia said on Sunday (November 8) its board was probing whether CEO Jensen Huang had been the target of a foreign intelligence effort, after a media report alleged he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing. Reuters Chief Technology Correspondent, Greater China Eduardo Baptista has more.
Short Link: https://lseg.group/4kHpemF

Video Transcript:

NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang has acknowledged to NVIDIA's board and all of its employees that he had an intimate relationship with the business executive. And this executive has been identified in media reports as Alice Huang, also known as "Huang Le." The more serious issue is not the affair itself, but rather the allegation in those reports that she was linked to a Chinese intelligence operation targeting him. NVIDIA says its board has opened an independent investigation into this reporting and the potential national security implications, and Jensen Huang has said that he would cooperate. It certainly is an unprecedented challenge to somebody that is seen as the key face of NVIDIA, and certainly somebody that has been instrumental to its rise. To put it simply, it clearly puts Huang under intense scrutiny. But it does not necessarily mean that he's about to lose his job. I think it all depends, really. On the one hand, he is NVIDIA's founder, chief executive, and central figure in its rise as the world's dominant supplier of AI chips, which are fundamental to the AI boom. But of course, the key question for the board will be whether its investigation concludes that there was any compromise of company information from Huang. And if it finds that there is no such impact, the board may conclude that continuity is more important for the company's interests. Of course, if there is a security lapse that is identified and the culprit is indeed Huang, the pressure on Huang would rise substantially. And this pressure would only increase if the investigation finds that Huang knowingly concealed this lapse. I think Washington would face a series of very difficult questions about who knew what, when they knew it, and what, if anything, they did with the information. Was Huang warned about this? Was NVIDIA warned? And did US officials assess whether sensitive commercial or even technological information could have been compromised? And there's a whole other dimension to this because NVIDIA's importance to US AI leadership and the export control tensions with China is so enormous that there could be questions about why there was no earlier public action or congressional notification.

I hope to have a great future here. NVIDIA has been coming to China for 30 years.

Remember that Jensen Huang is a vocal advocate for rolling back US export controls targeting Chinese access to NVIDIA's most cutting-edge AI chips. So, now, with this controversy, that advocacy will be seen in a much different light. And so, these are all questions for not just intelligence agencies, but also the Trump Administration, which has said publicly that it has been receptive to Jensen Huang's lobbying on this matter of US escort controls targeting China's access to NVIDIA chips. So, now that this whole debate has been intertwined with these underlying espionage allegations, it only remains to be seen how far NVIDIA's internal investigation will go and also how much congressional action will be taken against Huang and these allegations.

Dhaka

Dhaka, Nov. 9 -- As Bangladesh grapples with escalating violence and a deteriorating law-and-order situation, at least eight buses have been set ablaze and more than 50 crude bomb explosions rocked different locations across Dhaka over the past few days, according to a local media report.

It noted that a series of crude bomb explosions triggered panic at Dhaka University on Sunday evening, with multiple other locations across the capital also witnessing similar blasts.

The campus was still witnessing the evening rush when two loud explosions occurred in quick succession in the Teacher-Student Centre (TSC) area of Dhaka University.

Further blasts were reported near the administrative building, outside the VC Chattar and at the Mukti-Ganatantra Toron. Students also detained several people while they were attempting to flee the scene.

Meanwhile, crude bomb explosions were reported at several other locations across the capital, including outside the Criminal Investigation Department (CID) office in Malibagh, a report in Bangladeshi daily Dhaka Tribune stated.

The report further highlighted that in the early hours of Saturday, two motorcycle-borne individuals fled after detonating three to four crude bombs in quick succession at the Chowrasta intersection in the Jatrabari area of Dhaka.

Hours earlier, another bomb exploded outside the upazila parishad gate near Genda Bus Stand on the Dhaka-Aricha Highway in Savar, while eyewitnesses were unable to identify those responsible.

"Explosions are now occurring one after another across the capital and surrounding areas, in front of police stations, at police facilities, near important government buildings and on university campuses. Some attackers arrive on motorcycles, set off explosions and flee. In other cases, their movements are captured on CCTV. After each incident, police say they are investigating, conducting operations and trying to identify those responsible," the report mentioned.

"Questions remain, however, about who is behind the blasts and how directly the detained individuals are linked to them. Are police identifying and arresting the people who throw the bombs, or are arrests mainly of suspects and people accused of political affiliations, to fill arrest figures? And who is making and supplying the bombs, and directing the attacks?," it questioned,

Addressing the media at the DMP Media Centre on Sunday, Deputy Police Commissioner Md Akhtar Hossain said that police were closely monitoring incidents of crude bomb explosions and vehicle arson and conducting investigations into each of them.

Several suspects, including members of banned organisations and their affiliated outfits, have been taken into custody.

He said police suspected that a particular group was deliberately orchestrating sabotage activities to create panic among the public.

Speaking to Dhaka Tribune, Tawhidul Haque, a Dhaka University teacher and crime analyst, said that while arrests were essential to maintaining law and order, authorities must ensure that innocent people were not targeted and harassed merely on suspicion.

He stressed that no arrested person should be labelled a bomb thrower without sufficient evidence emerging from the investigation. Published by HT Digital Content Services with permission from IANS. The opinions expressed here are those of the author, a columnist for Reuters.

By Mike Dolan

Nov 9 (Reuters) - A nervy tech sector starts the week with a nearly 4% slide in AI chip giant Nvidia on a bizarre tale of an extramarital affair and spying allegations.

Nvidia boss Jensen Huang admitted to employees that he'd had an affair with a woman who news reports claimed was spying for China. The company said it was investigating those allegations and Huang's position may now be in the balance.

As Huang is a central figure in the whole AI buildout and an industry power figure in relations with Washington and governments around the world, markets may now be pricing the risk of his removal.

President Trump's initial response was to give Huang the benefit of the doubt, but he too faces questions about reports that he didn't act when intelligence originally briefed him on the situation several months ago.

Either way, the story will not calm anxieties in the AI investment world, which has just suffered its worst week in well over a year despite Friday's relief rally. It may also simply play into the hands of Nvidia competitors such as AMD and other leading chipmakers.

Asia stocks followed Friday's Wall Street tech bounce with gains of their own on Monday.

Markets were also digesting Friday's strong US payrolls report, where broad-based job gains came in at twice forecasts and lifted the three-month average payroll gain to more than 130,000 per month. Bets on another Federal Reserve interest rate rise next month pushed higher as a result.

Elsewhere, oil prices slipped on Monday after Trump indicated at the weekend that there would be no immediate re-escalation of the Iran conflict - a decision that follows the Republican Party's heavy defeats in last week's midterm elections.

In the background, Israeli opposition parties under Gadi Eisenkot have been given the first chance to form a government following the recent inconclusive elections there.

In China, there was a mixed picture on October inflation, with producer price inflation accelerating strongly but consumer price gains slipping back once more.

Otherwise, the release of US consumer price inflation data on Tuesday will top the economic release calendar this week as the earnings season starts to wind down.

CHART OF THE DAY

Nvidia shares fell sharply on Monday after news of the probe into Jensen Huang, which has put a spotlight on his future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

TODAY'S EVENTS TO WATCH

  • US 3-year note auction (1 p.m. EST)

  • Fed's Michelle Bowman, Chicago Fed's Austan Goolsbee and Richmond Fed's Thomas Barkin speak

NEWS BITES - PRIVATE COMPANIES (US)

+ THE FEDERAL RESERVE BANK OF CLEVELAND [1 Press Release]

+ CLEVELAND FED'S HAMMACK TIES DOLLAR STRENGTH TO RULE OF LAW, MARKET LIQUIDITY, AND CENTRAL BANK INDEPENDENCE

Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President and CEO Beth Hammack spoke on a panel at the SNB and Its Watchers Conference in Zurich, noting that monetary policy will likely need to move to a restrictive stance to bring inflation back to 2 percent in a timely manner.

On the dollar's international status, Hammack emphasized that the dollar's strength rests on fundamental qualities that include central bank independence so the Fed can deliver on our mission, and on having deep, liquid markets that allow investors to move in and out with ease. "The dollar's status depends on preserving the fundamental qualities that underlie its strength, qualities that provide a solid foundation for any currency. This includes maintaining central bank independence so we can deliver on our mission." She added that a reserve currency has to be more than trusted; it has to be available, in deep and liquid markets, so that investors can choose to move in and out of the currency as they see fit."

She also highlighted the Fed's independence and accountability to Congress as essential to sustaining global confidence in the dollar's inflation commitment and its role as a store of value. "The Fed's independence, along with its accountability to Congress, is critical to maintaining the world's confidence in our commitment to 2 percent inflation." "Delivering on our commitments is an important way the Federal Reserve helps the dollar remain a reliable store of value and that Americans can continue to reap the benefits of its global status." She also noted that digital currencies' price volatility makes them a less certain store of value than the dollar.

++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++++

The speculative dollar long position — derived from net contracts of International Monetary Market speculators in the euro, yen, pound, Swiss franc and Canadian and Australian dollars — slipped to $35.59 billion in the week ending November 3 from $37.44 billion the previous week. There is space for the dollar to climb as the current speculative long position is well below the $48.56 billion reached in July: the biggest long since the euro was introduced in 1999. The dollar posted its biggest gain in nearly six months on Friday as robust US jobs data pushed up bets for higher interest rates. The dollar index =USD, which tracks the greenback against six major currencies, on Friday saw the biggest one-day rise since June 17. Last week the dollar index failed to sustain brief breaks below the 101.266 Fibonacci level: a 38.2% retracement of the August-to-October rise from 98.558 to 102.94. That is a bear trap, which is set when a market breaks below a technical level but subsequently reverses and is usually a bullish sign. There is scope for dollar index gains to test the 102.49 October 29 high. A move above that level would unmask the 102.94 2026 peak posted earlier in October. https://tmsnrt.rs/4iwrJqLhttps://tmsnrt.rs/4j6dqt2

Mexico City.- Fiber optics in Mexico has been a key aspect of broadband competition for many years, so it is no surprise that the major companies listed on the local market – América Móvil, Megacable, and Televisa – are advancing in their deployment.

This is evident from the information they presented in the third quarter of this year, where all three companies listed on the Mexican Stock Exchange (BMV) showcased progress in their respective strategies.

For instance, América Móvil, the telecommunications giant of the Slim family , reported that by the end of September, 94% of its customers were already connected via fiber optics.

Regarding broadband in Mexico, I can share that we have maintained a good growth rate in recent quarters," stated Daniel Hajj, the company's CEO, during a call with analysts and investors.

Although company executives did not disclose specific figures during the conversation, América Móvil's data indicates that by the end of the quarter, broadband connections in Mexico reached 12.4 million , marking an annual growth of 4.8 percent.

Megacable Leads

Another company that demonstrated advancements in fiber optics deployment was Megacable , reporting that 89% of its subscribers were connected using fiber optic technology. This represents an increase from the third quarter of 2022 when the percentage stood at 82 percent.

As of September this year, Megacable's broadband subscribers totaled 6.07 million , reflecting an increase of 7.1% or 405,000 net additions compared to the previous year.

Finally, Grupo Televisa also made progress in expanding its network , but unlike its competitors, its measurement is based on its network rather than the number of customers.

Televisa's network encompasses over 20.1 million homes , with 67% of them already equipped with fiber optics, it added.

Coverage

Telecommunications users utilizing fiber optics, according to data from the companies themselves.

Company Score:

América Móvil 94%

Megacable 89%

Televisa 67%

Monterrey, NL.- The justification for tariffs on Mexico , partly due to the deficit faced by the United States, which President Donald Trump frequently reiterates, is a misguided measure, experts in foreign trade agreed.

Pedro Casas Alatriste, executive vice president and general director of AmCham Mexico , explained that the integration between the two countries is so extensive that Mexico should not be compared to other nations regarding the U.S. deficit.

This fixation on the deficit and how it is measured, particularly with Mexico, is fundamentally flawed. First, the trade relationship between Mexico and the U.S. is entirely different from the trade relationship the U.S. has with any other country in the world, not even with Canada," he stated.

Therefore, he insisted, measuring the U.S. deficit with Mexico when they have a co-production platform is akin to trying to measure the deficit between Texas and California, "that's how illogical it sounds."

The U.S. Census Bureau reported that from January to September of last year, Vietnam was the country with which the United States had the largest deficit, totaling $190.93 billion, while Mexico was second, with a deficit of $184.02 billion.

• El sector tecnológico sigue siendo el más importante del S&P 500, con una ponderación superior al 35 %
  • El sector ha subido más del 200 % en este mercado alcista
  • El PER del sector tecnológico cae por debajo de la valoración del mercado en general

Por Lewis Krauskopf

NUEVA YORK, 9 nov (Reuters) - A pesar del fuerte retroceso de los valores relacionados con la inteligencia artificial, el mercado bursátil estadounidense está preparado para apoyarse en el rendimiento de las acciones tecnológicas, y los inversores están en guardia ante los obstáculos que podrían entorpecer la negociación en las próximas semanas.

Una caída de un mes de duración en las acciones tecnológicas y relacionadas con la IA culminó esta semana con la mayor caída en un solo día del sector tecnológico del S&P 500 en más de seis años. A los inversores les preocupa que las victorias demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de mandato provoquen una ralentización del gasto en centros de datos, que ha sido el motor del repunte del mercado.

Sin embargo, a pesar de la caída, el sector .SPLRCT tecnológico sigue siendo, con diferencia, el sector más importante del S&P 500, el índice de referencia del mercado bursátil estadounidense. Aunque su influencia ha disminuido ligeramente, el sector tecnológico seguía teniendo una ponderación superior al 35 % en el S&P 500 .SPX al cierre del jueves.

«Dado que gran parte del sector tecnológico está muy vinculado a la inteligencia artificial, esto va a tener un impacto en todo el sector, y ese sector tiene un peso muy importante dentro del S&P 500», afirmó Robert Pavlik, gestor senior de carteras de Dakota Wealth Management. «Por lo tanto, la debilidad de la inteligencia artificial va a lastrar al sector tecnológico, lo que a su vez lastrará al S&P 500».

El porcentaje del sector en la capitalización bursátil del S&P 500 se mantiene por encima del nivel que alcanzó durante el apogeo de la burbuja de Internet en el año 2000.

El sector tecnológico por sí solo no refleja plenamente la influencia de la IA. Por ejemplo, tres hiperescaladores que invierten masivamente en centros de datos —Alphabet GOOGL.O, Amazon AMZN.O y Meta Platforms META.O — están clasificados en otros sectores.

La continua fuerte ponderación de la tecnología es una consecuencia de las enormes ganancias registradas por el sector durante el mercado alcista de la bolsa estadounidense que comenzó en octubre de 2022. A pesar del último retroceso del sector tecnológico, este ha subido más del 200 % durante ese periodo, casi el doble de la subida del S&P 500.

Algunas de las empresas más beneficiadas por la IA siguen registrando importantes ganancias en lo que va de año, a pesar de sus recientes caídas. Por ejemplo, las acciones de Sandisk SNDK.O habían subido alrededor del 250 % en 2026, mientras que Dell Technologies DELL.N registraba una subida de aproximadamente el 160 % y Micron Technology MU.O había subido un 140 %.

A medida que las acciones se recuperaban ligeramente el viernes, el S&P 500 cerraba con una subida de casi un 8 % en lo que va de año, con el sector tecnológico subiendo alrededor de un 11 %.

«Si alguien está en modo de recogida de beneficios, todavía hay beneficios que obtener», afirmó Chuck Carlson, director ejecutivo de Horizon Investment Services.

La caída del sector tecnológico también ha hecho que las valoraciones de las acciones parezcan —al menos a simple vista— más modestas. La relación precio-beneficio a futuro del sector tecnológico —basada en las estimaciones de beneficios para los próximos 12 meses— cayó hasta 17,1 el jueves, según LSEG Datastream, tras haber superado los 32 en octubre de 2025.

La relación precio-beneficio del S&P 500 en su conjunto se situó en 17,9. Esta semana ha sido la primera vez desde 2017 que la relación precio-beneficio del sector tecnológico ha caído por debajo de la del mercado en general.

La caída de las valoraciones significa que «podría decirse que… el mercado ya está descontando muchas malas noticias», afirmó Keith Lerner, director de inversiones de Truist Advisory Services.

«Nos estamos encaminando hacia una situación en la que una pequeña buena noticia podría tener un gran impacto», señaló Lerner en una nota el jueves.

Los inversores estarán atentos en las próximas semanas a una serie de posibles catalizadores que podrían impulsar el comercio de la IA en una u otra dirección:

** SALIDA A BOLSA DE ANTHROPIC: Los acontecimientos relacionados con la oferta pública inicial (OPI) del laboratorio de IA Anthropic están llamados a marcar el estado de ánimo en torno al sector de la IA. Reuters informó el jueves de que los posibles inversores están planteando dudas (link) sobre si la empresa podrá llevar a cabo su gira de presentación de la OPI la próxima semana a tiempo para su cotización en noviembre. Estos debates reflejan, en parte, el impacto de la fuerte caída de las acciones tecnológicas.

** RESULTADOS DEL SECTOR TECNOLÓGICO: Aunque ya se ha completado la mayor parte de la presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre, aún quedan algunos resultados clave por conocer. La empresa de servicios en la nube CoreWeave CRWV.O, que ha estado en el centro de las preocupaciones sobre la financiación de la expansión de la IA, presenta sus resultados el martes. Nvidia NVDA.O, referente del sector de la IA, lo hará el 17 de noviembre, mientras que Dell lo hará el 24 de noviembre.

** CONTEXTO MACROECONÓMICO: Los acontecimientos relacionados con el conflicto entre EEUU, Israel e Irán podrían influir de manera generalizada en la evolución de las acciones. Las expectativas de que el cambio en el Congreso pudiera suponer el fin del conflicto contribuyeron a la caída de los precios del petróleo esta semana, lo que a su vez benefició a las acciones. Sin embargo, los inversores se muestran cautelosos ante una posible escalada de las tensiones tras la celebración de las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Los inversores también siguen de cerca la evolución de las tasas de interés y la magnitud de las subidas que aplicará la Reserva Federal en los próximos meses para frenar la inflación. Una prueba de ello será el informe del Índice de Precios al Consumo de la próxima semana.

«Nos estamos encaminando hacia una situación en la que una pequeña buena noticia podría tener un gran impacto», señaló Lerner en una nota el jueves.

Los inversores estarán atentos en las próximas semanas a una serie de posibles catalizadores que podrían impulsar el comercio de la IA en una u otra dirección:

** SALIDA A BOLSA DE ANTHROPIC: Los acontecimientos relacionados con la oferta pública inicial (OPI) del laboratorio de IA Anthropic están llamados a marcar el estado de ánimo en torno al sector de la IA. Reuters informó el jueves de que los posibles inversores están planteando dudas (link) sobre si la empresa podrá llevar a cabo su gira de presentación de la OPI la próxima semana a tiempo para su cotización en noviembre. Estos debates reflejan, en parte, el impacto de la fuerte caída de las acciones tecnológicas.

** RESULTADOS DEL SECTOR TECNOLÓGICO: Aunque ya se ha completado la mayor parte de la presentación de resultados del tercer trimestre, aún quedan algunos resultados clave por conocer. La empresa de servicios en la nube CoreWeave CRWV.O, que ha estado en el centro de las preocupaciones sobre la financiación de la expansión de la IA, presenta sus resultados el martes. Nvidia NVDA.O, referente del sector de la IA, lo hará el 17 de noviembre, mientras que Dell lo hará el 24 de noviembre.

** CONTEXTO MACROECONÓMICO: Los acontecimientos relacionados con el conflicto entre EEUU, Israel e Irán podrían influir de manera generalizada en la evolución de las acciones. Las expectativas de que el cambio en el Congreso pudiera suponer el fin del conflicto contribuyeron a la caída de los precios del petróleo esta semana, lo que a su vez benefició a las acciones. Sin embargo, los inversores se muestran cautelosos ante una posible escalada de las tensiones tras la celebración de las elecciones de mitad de mandato. Los inversores también siguen de cerca la evolución de las tasas de interés y la magnitud de las subidas que aplicará la Reserva Federal en los próximos meses para frenar la inflación. Una prueba de ello será el informe del Índice de Precios al Consumo de la próxima semana.

• Las moscas estériles son la única herramienta probada para detener al parásito, peero aún hay escasez de suministro
  • EEUU registró dos nuevos casos de gusano barrenador en octubre
  • Se prevé que la planta de Texas que cría moscas estériles comience su producción en la primavera de 2027

Por Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas y Adriana Barrera

CIUDAD DE MÉXICO/WASHINGTON, 9 nov (Reuters) - Durante décadas, miles de millones de moscas estériles criadas en fábricas fueron dispersadas mediante aviones para mantener a raya al gusano barrenador del Nuevo Mundo, que ataca al ganado de Norteamérica. Esto controla la plaga porque los machos estériles se aparean con las hembras silvestres, cuyos huevos no llegan a eclosionar.

Pero esta estrategia solo funciona si el suministro de moscas nunca escasea.

Cuando el parásito rompió la barrera de moscas estériles en Panamá a principios de 2023, la región carecía de la capacidad para contenerlo. Los esfuerzos para aumentar la población de moscas siguen estando rezagados más de tres años después del brote, luego de que el parásito se propagara por México y Estados Unidos, según entrevistas de Reuters con 15 funcionarios y expertos, tanto actuales como anteriores, de Estados Unidos, México y Panamá.

Ante la escasez de moscas, la administración del presidente estadounidense, Donald Trump, cerró la frontera con México a la importación de ganado durante más de 15 meses a partir de mayo de 2025, interrumpiendo un comercio multimillonario. Cuando la frontera comenzó a reabrirse este año, se confirmaron decenas de casos en el ganado estadounidense.

México y Panamá producen actualmente alrededor de 150 millones de moscas estériles por semana, según datos de los gobiernos de Estados Unidos y México.

Eso representa menos de un tercio de los 500 millones semanales que se necesitaron durante la campaña en la década de 1960 para erradicar el gusano barrenador en Estados Unidos y que los expertos recomiendan como referencia para mantener la plaga confinada al sur de Panamá. Estados Unidos no cuenta con una planta propia de moscas estériles, y se prevé que la que se está construyendo en Texas comience a producir hasta la primavera de 2027.

Mientras tanto, el parásito se ha extendido por la mayor parte de México, con aproximadamente 51,000 casos confirmados. Estados Unidos ha registrado 120 casos hasta la fecha.

"No tenemos suficientes moscas", dijo Sonja Swiger, entomóloga de la Universidad Texas A&M. "Lo supieron enseguida".

Los esfuerzos por aumentar la población de moscas en varias etapas de la infestación se han visto obstaculizados por las transiciones políticas, retrasos en el financiamiento, obstáculos burocráticos y las crecientes tensiones entre Estados Unidos y México, dijeron a Reuters actuales y exfuncionarios.

La portavoz del Departamento de Agricultura de Estados Unidos (USDA por su sigla en inglés), Nancy McNiff, dijo en respuestas enviadas a Reuters por correo electrónico, que la agencia ha "actuado con urgencia y ha explorado todas las vías prácticas para introducir más moscas estériles en el campo lo antes posible".

Los portavoces de la presidenta mexicana Claudia Sheinbaum, de la Secretaría de Agricultura de México, de la Comisión Panamá-Estados Unidos para la Erradicación y Prevención del Gusano Barrenador del Ganado (COPEG) y del gobierno de Panamá no respondieron a solicitudes de comentarios.

ALARMA EN PANAMÁ

Las larvas del gusano barrenador desgarran los tejidos vivos y pueden matar a los animales que no reciben tratamiento. Una sola mosca puede poner hasta 3,000 huevos.

La liberación de miles de millones de moscas estériles cultivadas en fábricas llevó a la erradicación del gusano en Estados Unidos en 1966 y contuvo un brote en Florida en 2017.

A finales de febrero de 2023, las autoridades de la provincia panameña Darién se enfrentaron a unos 800 casos de gusano barrenador en la selva, que durante mucho tiempo había servido como la última línea de defensa de Norteamérica.

Mantener esa barrera es tarea de COPEG, la organización estadounidense-panameña que recibe la mayor parte de su financiación de Estados Unidos. En abril de 2023, decidió aumentar la producción de moscas estériles de 20 millones a 100 millones semanales, según declaró un funcionario panameño involucrado en la respuesta.

En julio de 2023, Panamá declaró la propagación del gusano barrenador como una emergencia, ampliando la liberación de moscas estériles, reforzando los controles ganaderos e intensificando la vigilancia.

En diciembre de 2023, la administración del expresidente estadounidense Joe Biden anunció una financiación adicional de casi 110 millones de dólares para la detección del gusano y la producción de moscas estériles en Panamá y otros lugares.

En noviembre de 2024, 19 meses después del inicio de la expansión, la planta de Panamá alcanzó los 100 millones de moscas por semana, según un funcionario panameño.

Ese mes, México confirmó sus primeros casos en Chiapas, un estado del sur que limita con Guatemala, y comenzó las liberaciones de la mosca.

Para entonces, las autoridades sabían que 100 millones de moscas estériles a la semana no eran suficientes, dijo a Reuters un funcionario panameño.

BRECHAS EN MÉXICO

Las elecciones en Estados Unidos y México ralentizaron la respuesta.

En septiembre de 2024, cuando la administración del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador se preparaba para entregar el poder, funcionarios salientes advirtieron a sus sucesores que la epidemia de gusano barrenador necesitaba atención inmediata, dijo un funcionario mexicano familiarizado con la respuesta.

La planificación inicial se centró en la reconversión de una planta de cría de moscas de la fruta ya existente en Metapa, Chiapas, en lugar de construir una nueva.

Según el funcionario, el traspaso de poderes retrasó el proceso entre tres y cuatro meses, mientras el nuevo Gobierno gestionaba la financiación y preparaba una propuesta para la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum.

En mayo de 2025, la administración Trump anunció una financiación de 21 millones de dólares para el proyecto Metapa. Funcionarios estadounidenses y mexicanos afirmaron que la planta podría llegar a producir entre 60 y 100 millones de moscas estériles por semana.

En febrero de 2026, las liberaciones de moscas estériles por parte de COPEG se trasladaron a la frontera entre Texas y México.

Según un funcionario del gobierno mexicano, Sheinbaum presionó a las agencias para acelerar el proyecto de la planta en México, buscando su inauguración en abril. Finalmente, la instalación se inauguró el 27 de junio, más de 18 meses después de que el país confirmara su primer caso de gusano barrenador.

Para entonces, el parásito se había extendido por 27 estados, llegando a importantes zonas ganaderas como Coahuila y Durango, en el norte de México, a cientos de kilómetros de la frontera sur.

UNA PLANTA EN TEXAS

El primer caso en Estados Unidos se confirmó el 3 de junio, pero el país aún no contaba con una planta de producción propia.

Según un exfuncionario de Biden, el USDA comenzó a hablar sobre una instalación en noviembre de 2024 y el personal de campo se reunió con grupos de la industria ganadera de Texas para tratar el tema de las ubicaciones ese mismo mes y en diciembre.

En junio de 2025, la secretaria de Agricultura, Brooke Rollins, declaró que el USDA estaba considerando la Base de la Fuerza Aérea Moore en Edinburg, Texas, sede de una antigua fábrica de moscas que había sido clave para el éxito de la campaña de la década de 1960.

En marzo, la administración Trump adjudicó un contrato de 610 millones de dólares a MA Mortenson para la construcción de las instalaciones, según consta en los registros públicos del contrato disponibles a través de una base de datos de gastos del gobierno estadounidense.

El USDA creía inicialmente que el proyecto podría tardar hasta cinco años, dijo la portavoz McNiff.

Funcionarios de la administración presionaron para acelerar el proceso. El USDA limitó las licitaciones para la construcción, argumentando que la licitación abierta podría retrasar un proyecto urgente, según los registros de gastos.

En una reunión de la Junta de Regentes de Texas A&M celebrada en septiembre, Rollins dijo que el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, había colocado el proyecto en el primer lugar de la lista de prioridades del Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército, reduciendo el plazo a unos 18 meses, o sea, al otoño de 2027.

John Bellinger, asesor de Rollins en materia de gusano barrenador y miembro del consejo de adminisracipon, afirmó que presionó para acelerar aún más el proceso. "Por solo 250 millones de dólares más, logramos adelantarlo al 1 de abril del próximo año", declaró Bellinger a los regentes, reduciendo aún más el plazo en aproximadamente seis meses.

Cameron Snyder, portavoz de Mortenson, afirmó en un correo electrónico que la empresa está comprometida a trabajar con el USDA y el Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército para entregar la planta rápidamente.

Hasta que la planta entre en funcionamiento, Estados Unidos seguirá dependiendo de moscas estériles producidas en otros lugares, aproximadamente 150 millones por semana en total, procedentes de las plantas de Panamá y Metapa, México.

Aunque Chiapas sigue siendo el estado más afectado de México, con alrededor de 8,200 infestaciones confirmadas, el USDA dijo que todas las moscas estériles producidas en Panamá y México se están liberando actualmente en el norte de México y Estados Unidos.

La estrategia pretende detener el avance del parásito hacia el norte antes de retroceder hacia el sur, lo que deja a gran parte de México y Centroamérica dependiendo de la vigilancia y el tratamiento, en lugar de la erradicación.

Incluso en los lugares donde se han logrado controlar los casos, la protección depende de que lleguen moscas estériles semana tras semana, dijo Swiger.

Algunos expertos estiman que podría llevar hasta una década repeler la infestación de gusano barrenador hacia Panamá. Esto deja la defensa de Norteamérica contra esta plaga dependiendo de una cadena de suministro biológico que, más de tres años después del inicio del brote, todavía produce solo una fracción de las moscas estériles necesarias.

(Reporte de Cassandra Garrison y Adriana Barrera en Ciudad de México y Leah Douglas en Washington. Editado por Emily Schmall y Suzanne Goldenberg.)

(( cassandra.garrison@thomsonreuters.com ))

Mantener esa barrera es tarea de COPEG, la organización estadounidense-panameña que recibe la mayor parte de su financiación de Estados Unidos. En abril de 2023, decidió aumentar la producción de moscas estériles de 20 millones a 100 millones semanales, según declaró un funcionario panameño involucrado en la respuesta.

En julio de 2023, Panamá declaró la propagación del gusano barrenador como una emergencia, ampliando la liberación de moscas estériles, reforzando los controles ganaderos e intensificando la vigilancia.

En diciembre de 2023, la administración del expresidente estadounidense Joe Biden anunció una financiación adicional de casi 110 millones de dólares para la detección del gusano y la producción de moscas estériles en Panamá y otros lugares.

En noviembre de 2024, 19 meses después del inicio de la expansión, la planta de Panamá alcanzó los 100 millones de moscas por semana, según un funcionario panameño.

Ese mes, México confirmó sus primeros casos en Chiapas, un estado del sur que limita con Guatemala, y comenzó las liberaciones de la mosca.

Para entonces, las autoridades sabían que 100 millones de moscas estériles a la semana no eran suficientes, dijo a Reuters un funcionario panameño.

BRECHAS EN MÉXICO

Las elecciones en Estados Unidos y México ralentizaron la respuesta.

En septiembre de 2024, cuando la administración del presidente Andrés Manuel López Obrador se preparaba para entregar el poder, funcionarios salientes advirtieron a sus sucesores que la epidemia de gusano barrenador necesitaba atención inmediata, dijo un funcionario mexicano familiarizado con la respuesta.

La planificación inicial se centró en la reconversión de una planta de cría de moscas de la fruta ya existente en Metapa, Chiapas, en lugar de construir una nueva.

Según el funcionario, el traspaso de poderes retrasó el proceso entre tres y cuatro meses, mientras el nuevo Gobierno gestionaba la financiación y preparaba una propuesta para la presidenta Claudia Sheinbaum.

En mayo de 2025, la administración Trump anunció una financiación de 21 millones de dólares para el proyecto Metapa. Funcionarios estadounidenses y mexicanos afirmaron que la planta podría llegar a producir entre 60 y 100 millones de moscas estériles por semana.

En febrero de 2026, las liberaciones de moscas estériles por parte de COPEG se trasladaron a la frontera entre Texas y México.

Según un funcionario del gobierno mexicano, Sheinbaum presionó a las agencias para acelerar el proyecto de la planta en México, buscando su inauguración en abril. Finalmente, la instalación se inauguró el 27 de junio, más de 18 meses después de que el país confirmara su primer caso de gusano barrenador.

Para entonces, el parásito se había extendido por 27 estados, llegando a importantes zonas ganaderas como Coahuila y Durango, en el norte de México, a cientos de kilómetros de la frontera sur.

UNA PLANTA EN TEXAS

El primer caso en Estados Unidos se confirmó el 3 de junio, pero el país aún no contaba con una planta de producción propia.

Según un exfuncionario de Biden, el USDA comenzó a hablar sobre una instalación en noviembre de 2024 y el personal de campo se reunió con grupos de la industria ganadera de Texas para tratar el tema de las ubicaciones ese mismo mes y en diciembre.

En junio de 2025, la secretaria de Agricultura, Brooke Rollins, declaró que el USDA estaba considerando la Base de la Fuerza Aérea Moore en Edinburg, Texas, sede de una antigua fábrica de moscas que había sido clave para el éxito de la campaña de la década de 1960.

En marzo, la administración Trump adjudicó un contrato de 610 millones de dólares a MA Mortenson para la construcción de las instalaciones, según consta en los registros públicos del contrato disponibles a través de una base de datos de gastos del gobierno estadounidense.

El USDA creía inicialmente que el proyecto podría tardar hasta cinco años, dijo la portavoz McNiff.

Funcionarios de la administración presionaron para acelerar el proceso. El USDA limitó las licitaciones para la construcción, argumentando que la licitación abierta podría retrasar un proyecto urgente, según los registros de gastos.

En una reunión de la Junta de Regentes de Texas A&M celebrada en septiembre, Rollins dijo que el secretario de Defensa, Pete Hegseth, había colocado el proyecto en el primer lugar de la lista de prioridades del Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército, reduciendo el plazo a unos 18 meses, o sea, al otoño de 2027.

John Bellinger, asesor de Rollins en materia de gusano barrenador y miembro del consejo de adminisracipon, afirmó que presionó para acelerar aún más el proceso. "Por solo 250 millones de dólares más, logramos adelantarlo al 1 de abril del próximo año", declaró Bellinger a los regentes, reduciendo aún más el plazo en aproximadamente seis meses.

Cameron Snyder, portavoz de Mortenson, afirmó en un correo electrónico que la empresa está comprometida a trabajar con el USDA y el Cuerpo de Ingenieros del Ejército para entregar la planta rápidamente.

Hasta que la planta entre en funcionamiento, Estados Unidos seguirá dependiendo de moscas estériles producidas en otros lugares, aproximadamente 150 millones por semana en total, procedentes de las plantas de Panamá y Metapa, México.

Aunque Chiapas sigue siendo el estado más afectado de México, con alrededor de 8,200 infestaciones confirmadas, el USDA dijo que todas las moscas estériles producidas en Panamá y México se están liberando actualmente en el norte de México y Estados Unidos.

La estrategia pretende detener el avance del parásito hacia el norte antes de retroceder hacia el sur, lo que deja a gran parte de México y Centroamérica dependiendo de la vigilancia y el tratamiento, en lugar de la erradicación.

Incluso en los lugares donde se han logrado controlar los casos, la protección depende de que lleguen moscas estériles semana tras semana, dijo Swiger.

Algunos expertos estiman que podría llevar hasta una década repeler la infestación de gusano barrenador hacia Panamá. Esto deja la defensa de Norteamérica contra esta plaga dependiendo de una cadena de suministro biológico que, más de tres años después del inicio del brote, todavía produce solo una fracción de las moscas estériles necesarias.

(Reporte de Cassandra Garrison y Adriana Barrera en Ciudad de México y Leah Douglas en Washington. Editado por Emily Schmall y Suzanne Goldenberg.)

• Sterile flies are the only proven tool to stop the parasite. But there are still supply shortages
  • US recorded two new cases of screwworm in October
  • Texas sterile-fly plant due to start production in spring 2027

By Cassandra Garrison, Leah Douglas and Adriana Barrera

MEXICO CITY/WASHINGTON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - For decades, planes dropped billions of factory-bred sterile flies to keep the flesh-eating New World screwworm out of North America’s cattle. That controls the pest because sterile males mate with wild females – whose eggs then fail to hatch.

But the strategy works only if the supply of flies never runs short.

When the parasite broke through a barrier of sterile flies in Panama in early 2023, the region lacked the capacity to contain it. Efforts to scale up the fly population still lag more than three years into the outbreak, after the parasite ripped through Mexico and into the United States, according to Reuters interviews with 15 current and former officials and experts in the US, Mexico and Panama.

Short on flies, the administration of US President Donald Trump closed the border with Mexico to cattle imports for more than 15 months starting in May 2025, disrupting a multibillion-dollar trade. As the border began to reopen this year, dozens of cases were confirmed in US cattle.

Mexico and Panama currently produce a total of about 150 million sterile flies a week, according to US and Mexican government data.

That’s less than a third of the 500 million per week it took during a 1960s campaign that eradicated the screwworm in the US – and that experts recommend as the benchmark to keep the pest contained to south of Panama. The US has no sterile-fly plant of its own, and one under construction in Texas isn’t expected to start production until spring 2027.

Meanwhile, the parasite has spread across most of Mexico, with about 51,000 confirmed cases. The United States has recorded 120 cases to date.

"We don't have enough flies,” said Sonja Swiger, an entomologist at Texas A&M University. “They knew that right away."

Efforts to make more flies at several stages of the infestation have been hampered by political transitions, funding delays, bureaucratic hurdles and rising US-Mexico tensions, current and former government officials told Reuters.

USDA spokesperson Nancy McNiff said in emailed responses to Reuters that the agency has “acted urgently and pursued every practical avenue to get more sterile flies into the field as quickly as possible.”

Spokespeople for Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum, Mexico’s agriculture ministry, the Panama-United States Commission for the Eradication and Prevention of Screwworm (COPEG) and Panama’s government did not respond to requests for comment.

ALARM IN PANAMA

Screwworm larvae tear through living tissue and can kill untreated animals. A single fly can lay up to 3,000 eggs.

Releases of billions of factory-made sterile flies eradicated screwworm in the US in 1966 and contained a flare-up in Florida in 2017.

In late February 2023, officials in Panama's Darien province confronted about 800 cases of screwworm inside the jungle that had long served as North America's last line of defense.

Maintaining that barrier is the job of COPEG, the US-Panamanian organization that gets most of its funding from the US. In April 2023, it decided to increase sterile-fly production to 100 million a week from 20 million a week, said a Panamanian official involved in the response.

By July 2023, Panama declared the spread of screwworm an emergency, expanding sterile-fly releases, tightening livestock controls and intensifying surveillance.

In December 2023, the administration of former US President Joe Biden announced nearly $110 million in additional funding for screwworm detection and sterile-fly production in Panama and elsewhere.

In November 2024, 19 months into the expansion, Panama’s plant reached 100 million flies a week, according to the Panamanian official.

That month Mexico confirmed its first cases in Chiapas, a southern state bordering Guatemala, and began releases.

By then, the authorities knew that 100 million sterile flies a week was not enough, the Panamanian official told Reuters.

GAPS IN MEXICO

Elections in the United States and Mexico slowed the response.

In September 2024, as President Andres Manuel Lopez Obrador’s administration prepared to leave office, outgoing officials warned their successors that the screwworm epidemic needed immediate attention, a Mexican official familiar with the response said.

Early planning centered on converting an existing fruit-fly plant in Metapa, Chiapas, rather than building a new plant.

The handover delayed the effort by three to four months, the official said, as the new government sorted out funding and prepared a proposal for President Claudia Sheinbaum.

In May 2025, the Trump administration announced $21 million in funding for the Metapa project. US and Mexican officials said the plant could eventually produce 60 million to 100 million sterile flies a week.

Sterile-fly drops from COPEG shifted to the Texas-Mexico border in February 2026.

Sheinbaum pushed agencies to accelerate Mexico’s plant project, seeking an April launch, according to the Mexican government official. In the end, the facility was inaugurated on June 27 – more than 18 months after the country confirmed its first screwworm case.

By then, the parasite had spread across 27 states, reaching major cattle-producing areas of Coahuila and Durango in northern Mexico, hundreds of miles from the southern border.

A PLANT IN TEXAS

The first US case was confirmed on June 3. But the US still had no production facility of its own.

USDA had begun discussing a facility in November 2024, and field staff met with Texas cattle industry groups about locations that month and in December, according to a former Biden official.

In June 2025, Agriculture Secretary Brooke Rollins said the USDA was considering Moore Air Force Base in Edinburg, Texas, home to a retired fly plant that had been key to the success of the 1960s campaign.

This March, the Trump administration awarded a $610 million contract to M.A. Mortenson to construct the facility, according to publicly available records of the contract through a US government spending database.

The USDA initially believed the project could take up to five years, spokesperson McNiff said.

Administration officials pressed to move faster. USDA limited bids on construction, arguing that open bidding could delay a time-sensitive project, according to the spending records.

At a September meeting of the Texas A&M Board of Regents, Rollins said Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth had moved the project to the top of the Army Corps’ priority list, cutting the timeline to about 18 months, or fall 2027.

John Bellinger, Rollins’ advisor on screwworm and a member of the board, said he pushed to move even faster. "For only $250 million more, we got it moved to April 1 of next year," Bellinger told the regents, further shortening the timeline by about six months.

Mortenson spokesperson Cameron Snyder said in an email that the company is committed to working with the USDA and the Army Corps to deliver the plant quickly.

Until the plant opens, the United States remains reliant on sterile flies produced elsewhere, roughly 150 million a week combined from the plants in Panama and Metapa, Mexico.

Although Chiapas remains Mexico’s hardest-hit state, with about 8,200 confirmed infestations, USDA said all sterile flies produced in Panama and Mexico are currently being released in northern Mexico and the US.

The strategy aims to stop the parasite’s northward advance before working back south, leaving much of Mexico and Central America reliant on surveillance and treatment, rather than eradication.

Even where cases have been suppressed, protection depends on sterile flies arriving week after week, Swiger said.

Some experts estimate it could take as long as a decade to push the screwworm infestation back to Panama. That leaves North America’s defense against the pest dependent on a biological supply chain that – more than three years into the outbreak – still produces only a fraction of the needed sterile flies.

(Reporting by Cassandra Garrison and Adriana Barrera in Mexico City and Leah Douglas in Washington. Editing by Emily Schmall and Suzanne Goldenberg)

Por Dhara Ranasinghe y Jiaxing Li

LONDRES, 9 nov (Reuters) - Las bolsas mundiales repuntaban ligeramente el lunes desde mínimos de seis meses, pero el ánimo seguía siendo frágil, mientras la caída de las acciones de Nvidia acentuaba la inquietud en torno a la inteligencia artificial tras el desplome mundial de los títulos tecnológicos la semana pasada.

Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O caían algo más de un 4% en las operaciones previas a la apertura, después de que una investigación interna sobre si su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera pusiera bajo escrutinio su futuro en el fabricante de chips de IA.

Al comenzar la sesión europea, los futuros del Nasdaq NQcv1 cotizaban sin cambios, tras haber operado antes en terreno negativo. Las acciones europeas .STOXX registraban ganancias modestas, mientras las bolsas asiáticas repuntaban y el Nikkei japonés .N225, que agrupa a grandes empresas, subía más de un 2%, con el descenso de los precios del petróleo ofreciendo cierto alivio a los mercados mundiales.

Las bolsas mundiales han estado bajo presión en las últimas semanas, con las inversiones vinculadas a la IA desplomándose en un contexto de tasas de interés al alza. A su vez, las amplias victorias demócratas en las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato de Estados Unidos agravaban los temores a una mayor regulación de la IA y los centros de datos.

Analistas dijeron que la cautela seguía marcando las perspectivas, con las ventas de acciones de Nvidia como la más reciente prueba para la confianza de los inversionistas.

"Por ahora, las repercusiones en el conjunto de la industria de los chips parecen relativamente limitadas, aunque el escándalo podría interrumpir el rebote tecnológico", dijo Susannah Streeter, estratega jefa de inversiones de la plataforma de inversión The Wealth Club.

El índice más amplio de MSCI de acciones de Asia-Pacífico, que no incluye a Japón, .MISX00000PUS subía un 1,25%, tras caer un 4,6% la semana pasada. El índice de referencia de Taiwán .TWII avanzaba casi un 5%, después de registrar la semana pasada su mayor descenso semanal en dos décadas.

Con todo ello, el índice mundial de acciones de MSCI .MIWD00000PUS ganaba un 0,4% y se mantenía por encima de los mínimos de seis meses registrados la semana pasada.

Los resultados que publicarán esta semana empresas tecnológicas como CoreWeave CRWV.O, Applied Materials AMAT.O y Cisco Systems CSCO.O pondrán a prueba la rentabilidad de sus ambiciones en IA, ante los enormes costos de expansión de la infraestructura.

CoreWeave se ha convertido en un barómetro de la inquietud de los inversionistas en torno a la IA, y el costo de asegurar su deuda contra un impago se ha disparado recientemente hasta niveles propios de emisores en dificultades financieras.

"El único factor fundamental que importa esta semana es el precio", dijo Chris Weston, director de análisis de la firma de corretaje Pepperstone, en Melbourne.

Por Dhara Ranasinghe y Jiaxing Li

LONDRES, 9 nov (Reuters) - Las bolsas mundiales repuntaban ligeramente el lunes desde mínimos de seis meses, pero el ánimo seguía siendo frágil, mientras la caída de las acciones de Nvidia acentuaba la inquietud en torno a la inteligencia artificial tras el desplome mundial de los títulos tecnológicos la semana pasada.

Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O caían algo más de un 4% en las operaciones previas a la apertura, después de que una investigación interna sobre si su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera pusiera bajo escrutinio su futuro en el fabricante de chips de IA.

Al comenzar la sesión europea, los futuros del Nasdaq NQcv1 cotizaban sin cambios, tras haber operado antes en terreno negativo. Las acciones europeas .STOXX registraban ganancias modestas, mientras las bolsas asiáticas repuntaban y el Nikkei japonés .N225, que agrupa a grandes empresas, subía más de un 2%, con el descenso de los precios del petróleo ofreciendo cierto alivio a los mercados mundiales.

Las bolsas mundiales han estado bajo presión en las últimas semanas, con las inversiones vinculadas a la IA desplomándose en un contexto de tasas de interés al alza. A su vez, las amplias victorias demócratas en las elecciones legislativas de mitad de mandato de Estados Unidos agravaban los temores a una mayor regulación de la IA y los centros de datos.

Analistas dijeron que la cautela seguía marcando las perspectivas, con las ventas de acciones de Nvidia como la más reciente prueba para la confianza de los inversionistas.

BUENOS AIRES, Argentina - Pope Leo XIV delivered a diplomatic but subtly strong critique of Argentine President Javier Milei's austerity measures and libertarian agenda as he arrived Sunday in Argentina, insisting that political leaders must put people, not the economy, first.

Leo used his first public speech in Argentina to lay out a vision of governance, democracy and society sharply at odds with Milei's, exposing differences over spending cuts, social justice and artificial intelligence that the government had sought to play down ahead of the visit.

"The economy must serve the person, not the person the economy," Leo told officials, diplomats and civic leaders upon his arrival in Buenos Aires from Uruguay.

Leo's visit to Argentina is by far the most politically delicate of his three-nation South American tour, and a place where Leo will also confront the complicated legacy of Argentine Pope Francis, who never returned home during his 12-year pontificate.

Milei, a self-described anarcho-capitalist, has staked his presidency on slashing public spending to tame inflation, while describing the notion of social justice as "a horror," a "moral aberration" and "theft" in recent speeches.

Much like its allies in the Trump administration, Milei's government has portrayed the cuts as part of a necessary reform process to remake Argentina's troubled economy and eliminate fraud and waste in the federal bureaucracy.

Ahead of Leo's arrival in Argentina, the first by a pope in nearly 40 years, Milei's officials had dismissed the prospect of a political clash.

"There's no way the pope is coming here to comment on local politics," Human Capital Minister Sandra Pettovello said in an interview with a Buenos Aires radio station last week. In a message welcoming Leo, Milei said he hoped the trip would "strengthen the faith, renew hope and bring a message of peace to all Argentines."

Leo took up that message of peace, opening with a call for gentler politics in deeply polarized Argentina. Democracy depends on "careful use of words" and "the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future," he said.

Milei's style is far more combative, costing him allies in Congress and public support. He posts dozens of times a day on social media, branding critics "traitors" and "human trash" and tagging posts #NOLSALP, a Spanish acronym for "We don't hate journalists enough."

Milei, who once called Francis the "representative of evil on Earth," paid homage to the late pope in welcoming Leo on Sunday. Interrupted by applause, he called Francis an "exceptional figure" and "undoubtedly the most important Argentine in history" whose teachings continue to resonate.

He also struck a rare conciliatory tone in welcoming politicians, diplomats and civil society representatives from across Argentina's ideological spectrum to Leo's ceremony.

"There are causes and occasions that transcend our differences," he said.

On the economy, Leo nodded to Milei's free-market instincts, urging Argentina to encourage "whatever creates opportunities" and "stimulates private initiative." But growth must also benefit "those who are disadvantaged," he said, including the unemployed, retirees and "all those who, despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

Milei's austerity drive has produced a rare budget surplus and slashed annual inflation from 200% to about 32%. But real wages remain below where they were when he took office in late 2023, and roughly 300,000 formal jobs have vanished. Retirees who say they can't afford medicine on an average monthly pension of $510 have protested outside Congress every Wednesday for more than two years. Milei has mocked the widespread complaint that families can't make it to the end of the month as "huge stupidity."

A missionary priest in Peru for two decades, Leo has embraced a pastoral style reminiscent of Francis, who as archbishop of Buenos Aires expanded the ranks of priests serving in the city's crime-ridden informal settlements.

Leo laid out a Christian vision of democracy, authority and economic progress that ran counter to Milei's. But he couched the implicit rebuke by referencing the church's social doctrine and papal pronouncements spanning more than six decades, invoking St. John Paul II, the last pope to visit Argentina, in 1987, among others.

That tradition also ran through Francis' papacy. His 2020 encyclical "Fratelli Tutti" criticized laissez-faire economics and defended social justice and workers' rights.

Argentina's bishops, many of them appointed by Francis, have become some of Milei's most persistent critics. Of the 44 documents on public policy published by the country's bishops' conference between January 2024 and September 2026, 42 criticized Milei's administration, on issues from poverty to migration, according to an analysis by sociologist Sol Prieto from Argentina's national research council.

Speaking to reporters after a Mass last month at the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Cathedral, Archbishop Jorge García Cuerva warned that Leo would find "a wounded Argentina, a divided Argentina."

Leo also took up the cause of Argentina's public universities, long a source of national pride and social mobility, whose funding cuts of about 40% since 2023 have united much of the country against Milei's fiscal shock therapy.

Giving young people a future in Argentina means "investing in education, vocational training, universities and research," he said.

Professors and students have repeatedly taken to the streets in mass protests, demanding the government honor a law passed by Congress to restore professors' salaries and boost scholarship and research funding after cuts that have driven thousands of academics from their jobs. Milei has refused to implement it, and the fight is tied up in court.

In a survey of nearly 1,200 final-year medical students and doctors in training, published last year by the Argentine Society of Medicine's research council, more than 80% said they had considered emigrating, and nearly a third had started applying for foreign citizenship.

"A nation must seriously ask itself where it has failed when its young people have to leave their homeland in order to make their dreams come true," Leo said.

Leo also said Argentina's natural resources must serve "the well-being of communities," language that could be read as a warning about Milei's bet on oil, gas and mining. To lure investment, Milei has loosened protections for glaciers that supply much of the country's water, and he has called human-caused global warming a "socialist lie."

Milei's push for investment has increasingly focused on artificial intelligence. With promises of minimal regulation and cheap energy, he is courting tech companies to build data centers in the southern Patagonia region. His government has also embraced AI for policing, which rights groups warn could enable mass surveillance.

Leo, who has made AI a signature concern of his papacy, warned on Sunday that rapid advances in the technology demand "careful consideration of the consequences of their application and the responsibilities of those who decide how to use them."

Associated Press writer Almudena Calatrava contributed to this report

Nov 07, 2026

On Jan. 1, President Donald Trump has threatened to double tariffs on automotive parts and vehicles from Canada. This would raise the current 25% tariff to 50% if the two countries cannot work out a deal.

The ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States has only been escalating over the last few weeks and months. Both countries have been hitting each other with tariffs on specific goods such as liquor, timber and most importantly, vehicles and automotive parts. A doubling increase on tariffs would make access to these parts more expensive and harder to get for not just both countries, but also Mexico.

The North American auto industry operates across U.S., Canadian and Mexican borders for different parts and assembly for just one vehicle. A large 50% tariff would make the manufacturing process financially and logistically difficult as it would be much harder for the parts to be accessed. Therefore, the best-case scenario for Canada and the U.S. is to include Mexico in their agreement to allow for the North American auto industry to continue to work together.

What does this 50% tariff mean for us, the consumers and customers? Automakers cannot afford to pay for that tariff, meaning the costs will pass directly to consumers. Many car companies manufacture their vehicles in the U.S. and Canada such as Ford, Honda, Toyota and others. These companies will have no choice but to pass on that tax to the consumers because their vehicles are heavily reliant on Canadian auto parts.

Canada has also stated that they will match U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar, meaning they too would instate a 50% on U.S.-made vehicles and auto parts. This would, in turn, not only hurt American consumers but also Canadian consumers as well. Of course, these retaliatory tariffs wouldn't just affect the auto industry, but many others like steel, aluminum, timber, liquor and electricity.

On Oct. 27, Honda Motor senior vice president executive Jennifer Thomas stated that 50% tariffs would be "really catastrophic for the industry." She has been an advocate for a trilateral deal and agreement between the U.S., Canada and Mexico in order to keep productions and costs down. Trade associations representing various car brands like Honda have also been advocating for a trilateral deal instead of trade wars between the two countries.

Thomas then said that she remains cautiously optimistic about the doubling of tariffs not taking effect. Recent reports have come out that the U.S. and Canada have reestablished trade talks which also adds to the optimism. The Trump administration has also been negotiating trade deals with other countries such as Japan and South Korea that already have 15% tariffs on vehicles put in place.

The trade war between Canada and the U.S. is not slowing down or stopping any time soon. The longer that talks and negotiations keep on continuing, the more costs are going to continue to rise for American consumers. We will have to wait and see how the negotiations play out before the start of the new year.

Beckett Showalter

lseg:urn:newsml:newsroom:20261109:nNRA2m.html_limpio: After Banco de México announced a 25 basis point cut to the reference rate last week, bringing it down to 6.25%, financial analysts consulted are seeing risks for the peso, as it could continue to lose ground against the dollar. Paulina Anciola, an analyst at Banamex, noted that with the cut from our central bank, they now project that the dollar will settle at 18.70 pesos by December, with upward risks. She emphasized that current levels remain consistent with the year-end forecast of 18.70 per dollar, although there are substantial upward risks due to Banxico's unexpected move. According to the specialist, the conditions for a more accommodative monetary stance were not met given a deteriorating outlook with rising inflation, a sharp increase in the National Producer Price Index (INPP), a depreciation of the peso, and stronger economic growth than previously estimated. Alejandro Padilla, chief economist at Banorte, highlighted that this week the dollar could fluctuate between 18.40 and 18.80 pesos. He pointed out that, in light of the challenging environment, our currency could range between 17.70 and 19.50 per dollar over the next 12 months, with a close of 18.40 for 2026 (average: 17.70) and 18.10 for 2027 (average: 18.15). This week, investors' attention will also be focused on the release of inflation data for October and industrial production figures for September that will be announced in Mexico. In the United States, inflation figures will also be released, with analysts expecting them to benefit from more stable gasoline prices.

Alejandro Padilla, chief economist at Banorte, highlighted that this week the dollar could fluctuate between 18.40 and 18.80 pesos. He pointed out that, in light of the challenging environment, our currency could range between 17.70 and 19.50 per dollar over the next 12 months, with a close of 18.40 for 2026 (average: 17.70) and 18.10 for 2027 (average: 18.15). This week, investors' attention will also be focused on the release of inflation data for October and industrial production figures for September that will be announced in Mexico. In the United States, inflation figures will also be released, with analysts expecting them to benefit from more stable gasoline prices.

• Nervous calm after Friday's Wall Street rally
  • Oil dips as Trump downplays risk of new Iran strikes
  • Nvidia shares fall sharply in pre-market trade

Changes dateline to London, updates throughout

By Dhara Ranasinghe and Jiaxing Li

LONDON, Nov 9 (Reuters) - World stock markets nudged up from six-month lows on Monday, but the mood was fragile as a fall in Nvidia shares added to the unease hanging over AI following last week's global rout in tech shares.

Nvidia NVDA.Oshares fell just over 4% in pre-market trading after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.

As European trade got under way, Nasdaq stock futures NQcv1 were flat, having traded negative earlier on. European shares eked out modest gains .STOXX as shares in Asia rallied and Japan's blue-chip Nikkei rose over 2% .N225, with a fall in oil prices offering some comfort to world markets.

Global stocks have been under pressure in recent weeks with the AI trade crumbling amid rising interest rates, and sweeping Democratic wins in the US midterm elections deepening worries about increased regulation of AI and data centres.

Analysts said the outlook remained cautious with the selloff in Nvidia shares the latest test of investor sentiment.

"For now, the repercussions across the wider chip industry look relatively limited although the scandal could disrupt the tech rebound," said Susannah Streeter, chief investment strategist at investment platform the Wealth Club.

MSCI's broadest index of Asia-Pacific shares outside Japan .MISX00000PUS rose 1.25% after sliding 4.6% last week. Taiwan's benchmark .TWII rose almost 5% after notching up its steepest weekly drop in two decades last week.

All this left MSCI's World Stock Index .MIWD00000PUS up 0.4%, holding above six-month lows hit last week.

Earnings reports due this week from tech companies including CoreWeave CRWV.O, Applied Materials AMAT.O and Cisco Systems CSCO.O are set to put the profitability of AI ambitions to the test amid the massive costs of the build-out.

CoreWeave has become a barometer of investor anxiety over AI, and the cost of insuring its debt has spiked into distressed territory recently.

"The only fundamental this week that matters is price," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

"You could easily see a lot of people going, 'You know what, now's the time to buy — blood on the streets. It's not as bad as everyone thinks,'" he said. "It will be driven by flow, and fundamentals will mean very little."

OIL PRICES EASE

Brent crude LCOc1 fell 2% to $96.29 per barrel after US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he was highly unlikely to order fresh attacks on Iran as long as talks to end the conflict progress.

Still, elevated oil prices continued to hang over the world economy.

China's factory-gate inflation accelerated to its fastest pace in more than four years while consumer inflation cooled in October, reflecting persistent cost pressures from higher oil prices despite weak domestic demand.

Market attention turned to US CPI numbers on Tuesday, with bets for a December Federal Reserve rate hike rising after Friday's blowout jobs report showed US employers added 165,000 jobs last month.

Money markets price in a roughly 80% chance of a quarter-point Fed rate hike in December. That pricing had briefly pulled back last week as the slide in tech shares raised economic growth worries.

The dollar was broadly soft after Friday's strong gains.

The dollar index =USD, which tracks the greenback against a basket of currencies of other major trading partners, was 0.3% lower at 101.88, having notched up its biggest one-day gain since June on Friday.

The euro rose 0.4% to $1.11 EUR=EBS, holding above its lowest level in roughly 1-1/2 years, which it hit last month.

In cryptocurrencies, bitcoin BTC= rose 0.5% to $74,397, after touching its lowest levels in over two months as investors fretted that a Democratic-controlled US Congress would toughen regulation on digital assets.

Elsewhere, several Chinese banks are sharply lifting dollar deposit rates, in some cases above US benchmarks, in unusually swift moves that bankers say are attracting cash and could temper gains for China's yuan, according to a Reuters report.

(Reporting by Dhara Ranasinghe in London, Jiaxing Li in Hong Kong and Tom Westbrook in Sydney; Editing by Joe Bavier)

(( Dhara.Ranasinghe@thomsonreuters.com ; +442075422684; ))
