Se añaden comentarios de Citi, Sequoia y Musk

9 nov (Reuters) - La junta de « NVDA.O » de Nvidia está investigando (link) si el director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, fue objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera, tras una noticia publicada en los medios en la que se alegaba que mantenía una estrecha relación con una empresaria china que pasaba información a Pekín.

A continuación se recogen los comentarios de analistas y figuras destacadas:

RYU YOUNG-HO, ANALISTA SENIOR DE NH INVESTMENT & SECURITIES:

«Parece que el Gobierno de EEUU llevaba varios meses al corriente del asunto relacionado con Jensen Huang, por lo que es poco probable que el impacto inmediato sea significativo.

«El mayor riesgo potencial para las empresas surcoreanas sería que una investigación prolongada o una revisión interna llevaran a Nvidia a retrasar sus decisiones de inversión.

«Si se retrasaran los envíos o los lanzamientos de productos de Nvidia, podría tener implicaciones más amplias para el sector de los semiconductores».

GARY BLACK, INVERSOR DE TESLA QUE GESTIONA FONDOS PARA THE FUTURE FUND LLC:

«Dudo que Jensen Huang pueda seguir siendo el director ejecutivo de Nvidia) (. Esto podría ejercer presión a corto plazo sobre las acciones de la segunda empresa más valiosa del mundo.

«No tiene ningún sucesor natural dentro de la empresa. Aunque Huang no ha cometido ningún delito ni infracción civil, su código de conducta y su criterio se pondrán en tela de juicio, lo que probablemente dará lugar a su destitución...

«Muchos gestores de carteras reducirán sus posiciones en (Nvidia) en las próximas semanas debido a la incertidumbre sobre quién podría suceder a Jensen».

EL PRESIDENTE DE EEUU, DONALD TRUMP:

«No he hablado con él sobre ello. Solo sé que es una buena persona, pero nunca se sabe lo que está pasando. Espero que todo vaya bien... Creo que es un tipo honorable».

BILL ACKMAN, DIRECTOR EJECUTIVO DE PERSHING SQUARE:

«No estoy sugiriendo que se le dé carta blanca. Si de verdad esto es algo más que una simple aventura, entonces es obviamente un problema grave. Me cae bien. Ha hecho mucho bien al mundo y espero que el daño en este caso sea mínimo. Es decir, espero que se trate simplemente de una aventura, no de un riesgo para nuestra seguridad nacional».

MOHAMED A. EL-ERIAN, EXCONSEJERO DELEGADO DE PIMCO:

«Aunque Nvidia ha intentado tranquilizarnos a todos, hay varios aspectos que tener en cuenta, empezando por el desafortunado momento en que se produce todo esto.

«Por ejemplo: la empresa es de importancia sistémica para el sector tecnológico, los mercados y la economía; a los inversores les cuesta valorar cuestiones relacionadas con las figuras clave y la gobernanza; y hay una dinámica cambiante en materia de seguridad nacional y geopolítica».

SHAUN MAGUIRE, SOCIO DE SEQUOIA:

Maguire afirmó que Huang «hizo algo increíblemente estúpido» que fue «perjudicial para Estados Unidos», pero que «Jensen es insustituible para el liderazgo estadounidense en IA».

El director ejecutivo de Tesla, Elon Musk, comentó «Estoy de acuerdo» en la publicación.

JOSH GILBERT, ANALISTA PRINCIPAL DE ETORO:

«Esta tormenta en la sala de juntas ha llegado en un momento brutal para el sector de la IA, pero los resultados de Nvidia del 17 de noviembre son la verdadera próxima prueba.

«Aunque es probable que la investigación afecte a la confianza del mercado, no alterará nada a largo plazo, a menos que provoque un cambio en la cúpula directiva, en cuyo caso la situación cambiaría por completo».

CHRIS WESTON, DIRECTOR DE INVESTIGACIÓN DE PEPPERSTONE:

«¿Será sustituido Huang? No, no creo que eso vaya a suceder.

«Creo que, dado que es como el padrino de la IA y, ya sabes, el pionero de lo que ha sido la mayor temática de inversión que hemos visto en una generación, quiero decir, creo que si realmente pensáramos que va a dimitir… las acciones caerían; sería una auténtica masacre, para ser sincero.

«Si se descubre que se confirma que ella es una espía, entonces, madre mía, la cosa se pone fea».

ATIF MALIK, ANALISTA DE CITI:

«Para los inversores, las cuestiones clave son probablemente las posibles implicaciones en materia de gobernanza, el aumento del escrutinio regulatorio y el cumplimiento de los controles de exportación en el flujo de chips H200 hacia China (<(el 1 % de las ventas de DC) y canalizados a través de otros intermediarios, así como (el impacto a largo plazo) en la estabilidad del liderazgo».

(En beneficio de las personas cuya lengua materna no es el inglés, Reuters automatiza la traducción de algunos artículos a otros idiomas. Adds Citi, Sequoia and Musk comments

Nov 9 (Reuters) - Nvidia's NVDA.O board is probing whether CEO Jensen Huang was the target of a foreign intelligence effort, following a media report alleging that he had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to Beijing.

Here are comments by analysts and prominent figures:

RYU YOUNG-HO, SENIOR ANALYST AT NH INVESTMENT & SECURITIES:

"It appears the US government had been aware of the matter involving Jensen Huang for several months, so the immediate impact is unlikely to be significant.

"The biggest potential risk for South Korean companies would be if a prolonged investigation or internal review were to lead Nvidia to delay its investment decisions.

"If Nvidia's product shipments or launches were to be delayed, it could have broader implications for the semiconductor industry."

GARY BLACK, TESLA INVESTOR WHO MANAGES MONEY FOR THE FUTURE FUND LLC:

"I doubt Jensen Huang will be able to remain as (Nvidia) CEO. This could put short-term pressure on the stock of the second most valuable company in the world.

"He has no natural successor within the company. While Huang has not committed any crime or tort, his code of conduct and judgment will be called into question, which will likely result in his removal ...

"Many portfolio managers will reduce their (Nvidia) holdings in the coming weeks as a result of uncertainty over who could succeed Jensen."

US PRESIDENT DONALD TRUMP:

"I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he's a fine person, but you never know what is going on. I hope everything's fine ... I think he's an honourable guy."

BILL ACKMAN, PERSHING SQUARE CEO:

"I am not suggesting he gets a free pass. If indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem. I like the guy. He has done a lot of good for the world and I hope the damage here is minimal. That is, I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security."

MOHAMED A. EL-ERIAN, FORMER PIMCO CEO:

"While Nvidia has sought to reassure us all, there are several layers here, beginning with the unfortunate timing.

"For example: The company is systemically important for tech, markets and the economy; Investors tend to struggle to price in key-person and governance issues; and there are fluid national security and geopolitical dynamics."

SHAUN MAGUIRE, SEQUOIA PARTNER:

Maguire said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America" but that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".

Tesla CEO Elon Musk commented, "I agree" to the post.

JOSH GILBERT, LEAD ANALYST AT ETORO:

"This boardroom storm has landed at a brutal time for the AI trade, but Nvidia’s earnings on November 17 are the real next test.

"While the investigation is likely to dent sentiment, it won’t alter anything long-term, unless it leads to a change at the top, at which point it becomes a completely different ball game."

CHRIS WESTON, HEAD OF RESEARCH, PEPPERSTONE:

"Will Huang get replaced? No, I don't think that's going to happen.

"I think given that he is like the godfather of AI and, you know, the OG of what has been the biggest investment thematic that we've seen in a generation, I mean, I think if we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down - it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest.

"If it is found out that she's confirmed as a spy, then, crikey, it doesn't go well."

ATIF MALIK, CITI ANALYST:

"For investors, key issues are likely potential governance implications, increased regulatory scrutiny and export-control compliance of the flow of H200 chips into China (<1% of DC sales) and routed through other intermediaries, and (long-term) impact on leadership stability."

(Reporting by Sumedha Mukherjee, Tom Westbrook, Brenda Goh, Danilo Masoni, Heekyong Yang and Jeanny Kao; Compiled by Anne Marie Roantree; Editing by Jamie Freed, Clarence Fernandez and Louise Heavens)

(( annemarie.roantree@thomsonreuters.com ; +852 97387151; Reuters Messaging: annemarie.roantree.thomsonreuters.com@reuters.net ))

Pope Leo XIV delivered a diplomatic but subtly strong critique of Argentine President Javier Milei's austerity measures and libertarian agenda as he arrived Sunday in Argentina, insisting that political leaders must put people, not the economy, first.

Leo used his first public speech in Argentina to lay out a vision of governance, democracy and society sharply at odds with Milei's, exposing differences over spending cuts, social justice and artificial intelligence that the government had sought to play down ahead of the visit.

"The economy must serve the person, not the person the economy," Leo told officials, diplomats and civic leaders upon his arrival in Buenos Aires from Uruguay.

Leo's visit to Argentina is by far the most politically delicate of his three-nation South American tour, and a place where Leo will also confront the complicated legacy of Argentine Pope Francis, who never returned home during his 12-year pontificate.

Milei, a self-described anarcho-capitalist, has staked his presidency on slashing public spending to tame inflation, while describing the notion of social justice as "a horror," a "moral aberration" and "theft" in recent speeches.

Much like its allies in the Trump administration, Milei's government has portrayed the cuts as part of a necessary reform process to remake Argentina's troubled economy and eliminate fraud and waste in the federal bureaucracy.

Ahead of Leo's arrival in Argentina, the first by a pope in nearly 40 years, Milei's officials had dismissed the prospect of a political clash.

"There's no way the pope is coming here to comment on local politics," Human Capital Minister Sandra Pettovello said in an interview with a Buenos Aires radio station last week. In a message welcoming Leo, Milei said he hoped the trip would "strengthen the faith, renew hope and bring a message of peace to all Argentines."

A call for civility in politics

Leo took up that message of peace, opening with a call for gentler politics in deeply polarized Argentina. Democracy depends on "careful use of words" and "the ability to see those who think differently as fellow citizens with whom we share a common future," he said.

Milei's style is far more combative, costing him allies in Congress and public support. He posts dozens of times a day on social media, branding critics "traitors" and "human trash" and tagging posts #NOLSALP, a Spanish acronym for "We don't hate journalists enough."

Milei, who once called Francis the "representative of evil on Earth," paid homage to the late pope in welcoming Leo on Sunday. Interrupted by applause, he called Francis an "exceptional figure" and "undoubtedly the most important Argentine in history" whose teachings continue to resonate.

He also struck a rare conciliatory tone in welcoming politicians, diplomats and civil society representatives from across Argentina's ideological spectrum to Leo's ceremony.

"There are causes and occasions that transcend our differences," he said.

On the economy, Leo nodded to Milei's free-market instincts, urging Argentina to encourage "whatever creates opportunities" and "stimulates private initiative." But growth must also benefit "those who are disadvantaged," he said, including the unemployed, retirees and "all those who, despite hard work, nonetheless struggle to meet their household's needs."

Milei's austerity drive has produced a rare budget surplus and slashed annual inflation from 200% to about 32%. But real wages remain below where they were when he took office in late 2023, and roughly 300,000 formal jobs have vanished. Retirees who say they can't afford medicine on an average monthly pension of $510 have protested outside Congress every Wednesday for more than two years. Milei has mocked the widespread complaint that families can't make it to the end of the month as "huge stupidity."

A missionary priest in Peru for two decades, Leo has embraced a pastoral style reminiscent of Francis, who as archbishop of Buenos Aires expanded the ranks of priests serving in the city's crime-ridden informal settlements.

Leo laid out a Christian vision of democracy, authority and economic progress that ran counter to Milei's. But he couched the implicit rebuke by referencing the church's social doctrine and papal pronouncements spanning more than six decades, invoking St. John Paul II, the last pope to visit Argentina, in 1987, among others.

That tradition also ran through Francis' papacy. His 2020 encyclical "Fratelli Tutti" criticized laissez-faire economics and defended social justice and workers' rights.

Argentina's bishops, many of them appointed by Francis, have become some of Milei's most persistent critics. Of the 44 documents on public policy published by the country's bishops' conference between January 2024 and September 2026, 42 criticized Milei's administration, on issues from poverty to migration, according to an analysis by sociologist Sol Prieto from Argentina's national research council.

Speaking to reporters after a Mass last month at the Buenos Aires Metropolitan Cathedral, Archbishop Jorge García Cuerva warned that Leo would find "a wounded Argentina, a divided Argentina."

Leo supports universities amid funding fight

Leo also took up the cause of Argentina's public universities, long a source of national pride and social mobility, whose funding cuts of about 40% since 2023 have united much of the country against Milei's fiscal shock therapy.

Giving young people a future in Argentina means "investing in education, vocational training, universities and research," he said.

Professors and students have repeatedly taken to the streets in mass protests, demanding the government honor a law passed by Congress to restore professors' salaries and boost scholarship and research funding after cuts that have driven thousands of academics from their jobs. Milei has refused to implement it, and the fight is tied up in court.

In a survey of nearly 1,200 final-year medical students and doctors in training, published last year by the Argentine Society of Medicine's research council, more than 80% said they had considered emigrating, and nearly a third had started applying for foreign citizenship.

"A nation must seriously ask itself where it has failed when its young people have to leave their homeland in order to make their dreams come true," Leo said.

A warning on natural resources and AI

Leo also said Argentina's natural resources must serve "the well-being of communities," language that could be read as a warning about Milei's bet on oil, gas and mining. To lure investment, Milei has loosened protections for glaciers that supply much of the country's water, and he has called human-caused global warming a "socialist lie."

Milei's push for investment has increasingly focused on artificial intelligence. With promises of minimal regulation and cheap energy, he is courting tech companies to build data centers in the southern Patagonia region. His government has also embraced AI for policing, which rights groups warn could enable mass surveillance.

Leo, who has made AI a signature concern of his papacy, warned on Sunday that rapid advances in the technology demand "careful consideration of the consequences of their application and the responsibilities of those who decide how to use them."

November 9, 2026 (University Wire via COMTEX News Network) --

On Jan. 1, President Donald Trump has threatened to double tariffs on automotive parts and vehicles from Canada. This would raise the current 25% tariff to 50% if the two countries cannot work out a deal.The ongoing trade war between Canada and the United States has only been escalating over the last few weeks and months. Both countries have been hitting each other with tariffs on specific goods such as liquor, timber and most importantly, vehicles and automotive parts. A doubling increase on tariffs would make access to these parts more expensive and harder to get for not just both countries, but also Mexico.The North American auto industry operates across U.S., Canadian and Mexican borders for different parts and assembly for just one vehicle. A large 50% tariff would make the manufacturing process financially and logistically difficult as it would be much harder for the parts to be accessed. Therefore, the best-case scenario for Canada and the U.S. is to include Mexico in their agreement to allow for the North American auto industry to continue to work together.What does this 50% tariff mean for us, the consumers and customers? Automakers cannot afford to pay for that tariff, meaning the costs will pass directly to consumers. Many car companies manufacture their vehicles in the U.S. and Canada such as Ford, Honda, Toyota and others. These companies will have no choice but to pass on that tax to the consumers because their vehicles are heavily reliant on Canadian auto parts.Canada has also stated that they will match U.S. tariffs dollar for dollar, meaning they too would instate a 50% on U.S.-made vehicles and auto parts. This would, in turn, not only hurt American consumers but also Canadian consumers as well. Of course, these retaliatory tariffs wouldn’t just affect the auto industry, but many others like steel, aluminum, timber, liquor and electricity.On Oct. 27, Honda Motor senior vice president executive Jennifer Thomas stated that 50% tariffs would be “really catastrophic for the industry.” She has been an advocate for a trilateral deal and agreement between the U.S., Canada and Mexico in order to keep productions and costs down. Trade associations representing various car brands like Honda have also been advocating for a trilateral deal instead of trade wars between the two countries.Thomas then said that she remains cautiously optimistic about the doubling of tariffs not taking effect. Recent reports have come out that the U.S. and Canada have reestablished trade talks which also adds to the optimism. The Trump administration has also been negotiating trade deals with other countries such as Japan and South Korea that already have 15% tariffs on vehicles put in place.The trade war between Canada and the U.S. is not slowing down or stopping any time soon. The longer that talks and negotiations keep on continuing, the more costs are going to continue to rise for American consumers. We will have to wait and see how the negotiations play out before the start of the new year.

Beckett Showalter

• La hija de Huang cancela su visita a Seúl para asistir al evento de IA de Nvidia
  • Elon Musk y Bill Ackman se pronuncian sobre la situación de Huang
  • Un analista advierte de que una investigación prolongada sobre Huang podría retrasar las inversiones de Nvidia
  • Los posibles retrasos podrían afectar a los precios de los chips de memoria, según un analista

Se añaden comentarios del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores chino y la cotización de las acciones en Fráncfort en los párrafos 6 y 11

Por Heekyong Yang, Kyu-seok Shim y Tom Westbrook

SEÚL/SÍDNEY, 9 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.Ocayeron bruscamente el lunes después de que una investigación interna (link) sobre si el director ejecutivo Jensen Huang había sido objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera pusiera en el punto de mira su futuro en la empresa fabricante de chips de IA.

La investigación interna se produjo tras una noticia publicada en los medios de comunicación según la cual Huang mantenía una estrecha relación con una empresaria china que, supuestamente, pasaba información a Pekín. Huang comunicó a los empleados de Nvidia (link) que había sido infiel a su esposa, sin revelar detalles de la relación.

La investigación, anunciada el domingo, ha puesto el foco en el futuro de Huang, dada la posición de Nvidia como el fabricante de chips más valioso del mundo y el papel del director ejecutivo (link) como el vendedor más prolífico del auge de la IA.

Huang, con su característica chaqueta de cuero, goza de un estatus de estrella del rock en todo el mundo, especialmente en Asia, donde a menudo se mezcla libremente con sus admiradores, haciéndose selfies y firmando autógrafos para sus devotos seguidores.

Las repercusiones de la investigación se extendieron a Corea del Sur, donde Madison Huang, hija de Huang y ejecutiva de Nvidia, canceló una visita prevista a Seúl para asistir a una conferencia de Nvidia que debía comenzar el lunes, según las empresas con las que tenía programadas reuniones.

Las acciones de Nvidia se desplomaron más de un 6 % en la bolsa de Fráncfort, prolongando la ola de ventas de la semana pasada y empujando el valor a nuevos mínimos de varios meses. A esos niveles, el fabricante de chips podría perder unos 270.000 millones de dólares respecto a su precio de cierre del viernes, según LSEG Datastream.

«Probablemente, el mercado te está diciendo ahora que esto no beneficia en absoluto a la acción en un momento en el que hay muchas conjeturas sobre laexpansión de los centros de datos», afirmó Chris Weston, director de investigación de la correduría Pepperstone en Melbourne.

Sin embargo, Weston señaló que no creía que Huang, a quien describió como el «padrino de la IA», fuera a ser sustituido.

«Si realmente pensáramos que iba a dimitir… las acciones estarían a la baja; sería una auténtica masacre, para ser sinceros», afirmó.

El New York Times informó el mes pasado (link) de que Huang mantenía una relación con Alice Huang, una antigua ejecutiva —sin parentesco alguno con él— de la empresa Megaspeed, con sede en Singapur, a quien las autoridades estadounidenses investigaron y concluyeron que era un agente de los servicios de inteligencia chinos.

«La denominada narrativa del espía chino no es más que una acusación infundada, una calumnia y una campaña de desprestigio», declaró a los periodistas en Pekín el portavoz del Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores chino, Guo Jiakun.

Megaspeed no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios el lunes, día festivo en Singapur.

Alice Huang no respondió al New York Times el mes pasado cuando este informó por primera vez de su relación con Huang, y Reuters no pudo determinar su paradero para recabar sus comentarios el lunes.

SIN EFECTOS EN LOS SOCIOS ASIÁTICOS

Las acciones de los principales proveedores asiáticos de chips de Nvidia —TSMC 2330.TW, Samsung Electronics <005930.KS> y SK Hynix 000660.KS, se recuperaron el lunes tras la ola de ventas de la semana pasada en los valores relacionados con la IA. Las acciones de TSMC subieron un 6,5 %, mientras que las de Samsung y SK Hynix lo hicieron un 2,9 % y un 4,7 %, respectivamente.

Algunas figuras destacadas se pronunciaron sobre la confesión de Huang. El inversor multimillonario Bill Ackman, fundador de Pershing Square Capital Management, afirmó en X que el director ejecutivo de Nvidia era «una persona increíble», pero que si «de verdad esto es más que una simple aventura, entonces es obviamente un problema grave».

«Espero que se trate simplemente de una aventura amorosa, y no de un riesgo para nuestra seguridad nacional», añadió.

El director ejecutivo de Tesla, Elon Musk (link), comentó «Estoy de acuerdo» en una publicación del socio de Sequoia, Shaun Maguire, en la que se decía que Huang «había hecho algo increíblemente estúpido» que era «malo para Estados Unidos», pero que «Jensen es insustituible para el liderazgo estadounidense en IA».

El presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump (link), declaró el domingo que no había hablado con Huang sobre las acusaciones, pero lo calificó de «buena persona» (link). «Espero que todo vaya bien. Ha hecho un trabajo increíble», añadió.

Cuando se le preguntó si creía que debería haber tomado medidas al recibir la información de los servicios de inteligencia, Trump respondió: «No, no lo creo. Creo que es un tipo honorable. Probablemente tenga una explicación para ello. Hay que escucharla».

El New York Times informó de que Trump fue informado de las conclusiones de los servicios de inteligencia hace aproximadamente un año y decidió no hacer nada al respecto.

VISITA CANCELADA

Madison Huang tenía previsto inicialmente visitar la startup surcoreana de IA Rebellions y celebrar una sesión de preguntas y respuestas con Kakao Mobility. Rebellions afirmó que los eventos se cancelaron debido a «circunstancias internas inevitables en Nvidia».

El Nvidia AI Day Seoul, un evento de dos días que se espera que atraiga a unos 2.000 participantes para debatir sobre IA física, IA agentiva e infraestructura, se celebrará según lo previsto, según los medios surcoreanos. Nvidia no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios.

Los analistas señalaron que una investigación prolongada o una revisión interna podrían retrasar las decisiones de inversión o los lanzamientos de productos de Nvidia, lo que tendría implicaciones más amplias para el sector de los semiconductores.

Ryu Young-ho, analista sénior de NH Investment & Securities, señaló que los rivales de Nvidia, entre ellos Advanced Micro Devices AMD.O, podrían atraer una mayor atención a corto plazo, lo que podría situar en el punto de mira a Samsung, que mantiene estrechos vínculos comerciales con AMD.

No obstante, señaló que los productos de Nvidia serían difíciles de sustituir, lo que limitaría el impacto potencial, aunque los envíos a China podrían sufrir nuevos retrasos dependiendo de cómo evolucione la situación.

El viceministro de Ciencia de Corea del Sur declaró el lunes que el Gobierno no esperaba interrupciones en las entregas contratadas de unidades de procesamiento gráfico de Nvidia (link), a pesar de los problemas a los que se enfrenta actualmente la empresa.

(En beneficio de las personas cuya lengua materna no es el inglés, Reuters automatiza la traducción de algunos artículos a otros idiomas. Dado que la traducción automática puede cometer errores o no incluir el contexto necesario, Reuters no se hace responsable de la exactitud del texto traducido automáticamente, sino que proporciona estas traducciones únicamente para conveniencia de sus lectores. Reuters no se hace responsable de los daños o pérdidas —del tipo que sean— causados por el uso de la función de traducción automática.)

• Huang's daughter cancels Seoul visit for Nvidia AI event
  • Elon Musk, Bill Ackman weigh in on Huang's situation
  • Analyst warns prolonged Huang probe could delay Nvidia investments
  • Potential delays could affect memory chip prices, analyst says

Adds Chinese Foreign Ministry comment, trading in Frankfurt shares in paragraphs 6 and 11

By Heekyong Yang, Kyu-seok Shim and Tom Westbrook

SEOUL/SYDNEY, Nov 9 (Reuters) - Nvidia NVDA.O shares fell sharply on Monday after an internal investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny.

The internal probe followed a media report that Huang had a close relationship with a Chinese businesswoman who allegedly passed information to Beijing. Huang told Nvidia's employees that he had been unfaithful to his wife, without disclosing details of the relationship.

The investigation, announced on Sunday, has put a spotlight on Huang's future given Nvidia's status as the world's most valuable chipmaker and the CEO's role as the most prolific salesman of the AI boom.

The leather-jacketed Huang enjoys rock-star status worldwide, particularly in Asia, where he often mingles freely with fans, taking selfies and signing autographs for his devoted followers.

The fallout from the probe extended to South Korea, where Madison Huang, Huang's daughter and an Nvidia executive, cancelled a planned visit to Seoul for an Nvidia conference that was set to begin on Monday, according to companies she had been scheduled to meet.

Nvidia's shares tumbled more than 6% in Frankfurt trading, extending last week's selloff and pushing the stock to fresh multi-month lows. At those levels, the chipmaker stood to lose about $270 billion from its closing price on Friday, according to LSEG Datastream.

"The market's probably telling you now this does no favours to the stock whatsoever in a time when there's a lot of conjecture as to the build-out of data centres," said Chris Weston, head of research at brokerage Pepperstone in Melbourne.

But Weston said he did not think Huang, whom he described as the "godfather of AI", would be replaced.

"If we genuinely thought he was going to step down ... the stock would be down — it would be an absolute bloodbath, to be honest,” he said.

The New York Times reported last month that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an unrelated former executive of Singapore-based company Megaspeed, who US authorities investigated and concluded was a Chinese intelligence asset.

"The so-called Chinese spy narrative is purely a groundless accusation, slander, and a smear," Chinese Foreign Ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun told reporters in Beijing.

Megaspeed did not respond immediately to a request for comment on Monday, a public holiday in Singapore.

Alice Huang did not respond to the New York Times last month when it first reported her relationship with Huang, and Reuters could not determine her location to seek comment on Monday.

ASIA PARTNERS UNAFFECTED

Shares in Nvidia's key Asian chip suppliers TSMC 2330.TW, Samsung Electronics <005930.KS> and SK Hynix 000660.KS rebounded on Monday after last week's selloff of AI-related stocks. TSMC shares jumped 6.5%, while those in Samsung and SK Hynix climbed 2.9% and 4.7%, respectively.

Some prominent figures weighed in on Huang's admission. Billionaire investor Bill Ackman, founder of Pershing Square Capital Management, said on X that the Nvidia CEO was an "incredible human," but if "indeed this is more than an affair, then it is obviously a real problem."

"I am hoping for a simple affair, not a risk to our national security," he added.

Tesla CEO Elon Musk commented, "I agree", on a post by Sequoia partner Shaun Maguire that said Huang "did something incredibly dumb" that was "bad for America" but that "Jensen is irreplaceable for America's AI leadership".

US President Donald Trump said on Sunday he had not spoken to Huang about the allegations, but called him a fine person. "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job," he added.

When asked if he believed he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed about it, Trump said: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honorable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it."

The New York Times reported that Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings roughly a year ago and chose not to do anything with the information.

CANCELLED VISIT

Madison Huang had initially planned to visit South Korean AI startup Rebellions and hold a question-and-answer session with Kakao Mobility. Rebellions said the events were cancelled due to "unavoidable internal circumstances at Nvidia."

Nvidia AI Day Seoul, a two-day event expected to draw about 2,000 participants to discuss physical AI, agentic AI and infrastructure, will proceed as planned, according to South Korean media. Nvidia did not respond immediately to a request for comment.

Analysts said a prolonged investigation or internal review could potentially delay Nvidia's investment decisions or product launches, with broader implications for the semiconductor industry.

Ryu Young-ho, a senior analyst at NH Investment & Securities, said Nvidia's rivals, including Advanced Micro Devices AMD.O, could attract greater attention in the short term, potentially putting Samsung, which has close business ties with AMD, in the spotlight.

Still, he said Nvidia's products would be difficult to replace, limiting the potential impact, although shipments to China could face further delays depending on how the situation developed.

South Korea's deputy science minister said on Monday the government expected no disruptions to contracted deliveries of Nvidia graphics processing units despite issues currently facing the company.

(Reporting by Kyu-seok Shim and Heekyong Yang in Seoul, Tom Westbrook in Sydney, Roger Tung and Ben Blanchard in Taipei, Danilo Masoni in Milan; Writing by Brenda Goh; Editing by Ed Davies and Jamie Freed)

9 nov - Bienvenidos a la página de cobertura en tiempo real de los mercados, ofrecida por los periodistas de Reuters. Pueden compartir sus opiniones con nosotros en markets.research@thomsonreuters.com

ANTES DE LA APERTURA: LOS FUTUROS EUROPEOS SE DEBILITAN, NVIDIA FRENA EL REPUNTE TECNOLÓGICO

Los futuros europeos se mostraban ligeramente a la baja el lunes, al recuperarse en cierta medida la calma en los mercados tras una semana agitada, marcada por la preocupación de que una victoria arrolladora de los demócratas en las elecciones de mitad de mandato de EEUU pudiera dar lugar a una regulación más estricta de la inteligencia artificial.

Los inversores se lanzaron a por las maltrechas acciones tecnológicas tras el repunte del viernes en Wall Street. Las bolsas asiáticas se recuperaron (link), y los fabricantes de chips impulsaron el índice de referencia de Taiwán .TWII un 5 % después de que las autoridades activaran medidas para estabilizar el mercado bursátil.

Sin embargo, la confianza siguió siendo frágil después de que una investigación interna de Nvidia (link) NVDA.O sobre si el director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera pusiera en el punto de mira su futuro en el fabricante de chips de IA. Sus acciones cayeron un 6 % en Fráncfort.

Los contratos sobre el índice de referencia EuroSTOXX50 .STOXX50E cayeron un 0,2 %, mientras que los futuros del Nasdaq NQc1 y del S&P 500 ESc1 bajaron un 0,7 % y se mantuvieron estables, respectivamente. Por su parte, los precios del petróleo (link) cayeron después de que el presidente Donald Trump restara importancia a la probabilidad de nuevos ataques contra Irán.

En cuanto a las noticias empresariales europeas, los bancos acapararon la atención.

El Banco BPM (link) BAMI.MI se encaminaba hacia un fuerte repunte después de que Crédit Agricole CAGR.PA propusiera fusionar la entidad italiana con su filial local, mientras que UniCredit (link) CRDI.MI elevó su objetivo de beneficios mientras se prepara para tomar el control de Commerzbank CBKG.DE.

La revisión al alza de JP Morgan a «sobreponderar» impulsó al grupo de software SAP SAPG.DE casi un 2 % en las operaciones previas a la apertura del mercado. Hochtief (link) HOTG.DE sufrió una fuerte caída después de que la constructora española ACS ACS.MC desmintiera los planes de adquirir su filial alemana.

Más tarde, la atención de los inversores volverá a centrarse en el sector tecnológico, ya que se espera que los resultados de CoreWeave CRWV.O, Applied Materials AMAT.O y Cisco Systems CSCO.O aporten nueva información sobre si el elevado gasto relacionado con la inteligencia artificial se está traduciendo en beneficios.

Los datos del IPC de EEUU del martes también podrían poner a prueba a los mercados.

(Danilo Masoni)

Welcome to the home for real-time coverage of markets brought to you by Reuters reporters. You can share your thoughts with us at markets.research@thomsonreuters.com

BEFORE THE BELL: EUROPE FUTURES SOFT, NVIDIA DENTS TECH BOUNCE

European futures were just slightly lower on Monday as a degree of calm returned to markets after a bruising week driven by concerns that a Democratic sweep in the US midterm elections could lead to tighter AI regulation.

Investors picked up battered tech stocks after Friday's bounce on Wall Street. Asian shares rebounded, with chipmakers lifting the Taiwan benchmark .TWII by 5% after autorities activated measures to stabilise the stock market.

Sentiment however remained fragile after an internal NvidiaNVDA.O investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang had been targeted by a foreign intelligence effort put his future at the AI chipmaker under scrutiny. Its shares fell 6% in Frankfurt.

Contracts on the EuroSTOXX50 .STOXX50E benchmark fell 0.2%, while Nasdaq NQc1 and S&P 500 ESc1 futures were down 0.7% and flat, respectively. Oil prices, meanwhile, fell after President Donald Trump downplayed the likelihood of new strikes on Iran.

In European corporate news, banks were in focus.

Banco BPMBAMI.MI was set for a strong rally after Credit Agricole CAGR.PA proposed merging the Italian lender with its local unit, while UniCreditCRDI.MI raised its profit goal as it prepares to take control of Commerzbank CBKG.DE.

A JP Morgan upgrade to overweight lifted software group SAP SAPG.DE by almost 2% in premarket trade. HochtiefHOTG.DE was called down sharply after Spanish builder ACS ACS.MC denied plans to take over its German unit.

Investors' attention will later turn back to tech, with results from CoreWeave CRWV.O, Applied Materials AMAT.O and Cisco Systems CSCO.O expected to provide new insight into whether hefty AI-related spending is translating into profits.

US CPI data on Tuesday could also test markets.

(Danilo Masoni)

The author is a Reuters Breakingviews columnist. The opinions expressed are her own.

By Robyn Mak

HONG KONG, Nov 9 (Reuters Breakingviews) - Of all the crazes spawned by the AI boom, the one that people will come to regret the most may be "Jensanity". Nvidia NVDA.O founder, boss and self-styled nerd-turned-billionaire Jensen Huang has been fawned over like a rock star. His extra-marital affair with an alleged Chinese spy now puts an intense spotlight on governance at the $4.5 trillion chipmaker, which is a critical supplier to Anthropic and other AI leaders. While the distraction may help rival Huawei, Beijing has more to lose if Washington tightens export controls.

After insisting last month that his ties to Alice Huang - a former executive of Singapore-based customer Megaspeed - were "completely normal", the Nvidia boss did a stunning U-turn on Sunday, admitting his unfaithfulness to his wife and agreeing to cooperate in a board-led probe on whether he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. The fallout will have sweeping consequences at what is arguably the world’s most important company in the AI boom.

At the very least, it will disrupt business as usual. Nvidia says its boss is committed to lead "without interruption" but that looks challenging: Under Nvidia's "extreme co-design" workflow, Huang oversees more than 60 direct reports, an extraordinarily large number for any manager. At worst, it could turn into a full blown leadership crisis. Nvidia relies heavily on Huang even though, as of March, he owned just 3.58% of the company. There's no super voting stock, and although both his children are in the business, Nvidia has no obvious successor should the board decide he has to go.

Nvidia's dealings with China will also be put under a microscope. The company's sales to the People's Republic, which are mostly comprised of less advanced processors and non-AI chips, nearly doubled to roughly $8 billion in the latest quarter, accounting for 8% of the total. Heightened scrutiny may ultimately result in Chinese firms moving faster toward domestic alternatives from Huawei and smaller challengers that are narrowing the technological gap in processors used for large-language models, robotics and cars. They are already steadily eroding the hold Nvidia has on the $90 billion AI chip market in China by developing their own software and easing migration from the US titan's products.

Still, the fallout may end up hurting China's AI prospects more than it helps. Tech titans from Alibaba 9988.HK to ByteDance legally access processors that are off limits to them in the People's Republic via overseas data centres operated by neoclouds like Megaspeed, which is active in Southeast Asia. But US authorities are also increasingly uncovering illegal chip smuggling operations via the region, casting doubt on how well export controls are enforced. The New York Times reported last year that Megaspeed, which bought billions of dollars of Nvidia processors, was under investigation for diverting chips to China. At the time, Huang insisted Nvidia had repeatedly sampled data centres around the world and found no diversion.

His affair will raise awkward questions over whether his company was negligent, turned a blind eye or worse. Regardless, Washington will now face more pressure to take a harder stance on enforcing chip curbs, and perhaps even close legal workarounds.

Follow Robyn Mak on X.

CONTEXT NEWS

Nvidia's board of directors on November 8 said it is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent media reporting on whether its founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort.

On the same day, Huang apologised for being unfaithful to his wife and said he was committed to winning back the confidence of Nvidia's board, partners and shareholders. The company added that he is committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption.

On November 6, the Financial Times reported that the US believed Huang had a romantic relationship with a Chinese woman who was recruited to spy for China’s Ministry of State Security intelligence agency. American officials this year wrote a memo, based on information from US intelligence, which said the Nvidia boss had been romantically involved with Alice Huang, who was at the time an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based customer, the FT report added, citing people familiar with the document.

Alice Huang is not related to Jensen Huang. China’s foreign ministry did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment.

In late October, the New York Times reported that American officials had concluded Alice Huang was a Chinese intelligence asset and had developed a "close relationship" with Jensen Huang, citing sources. A year earlier, the publication reported that US Commerce Department officials had been investigating Megaspeed for helping Chinese companies sidestep American export restrictions, citing sources.

Nvidia's CEO told Bloomberg News last month that his relationship and interactions with Alice Huang were related to Megaspeed and were "completely normal and not unusual".

(Editing by Una Galani; Production by Eileen Soreng)

09 November 2026

Great Southern Copper plc

("GSC" or the "Company")

Diamond Drilling Commences at Artemisa Cu-Mo Prospect

Scout RC Drilling Results Vector Porphyry Cu Exploration to La Colorada Lithocap, Especularita

Great Southern Copper plc (LSE: GSCU), the company focused on copper-gold-silver exploration in Chile, is pleased to announce the start of drilling targeting Cu-Mo mineralisation discovered in Reverse Circulation ("RC") drilling at the Artemisa prospect, plus provide an update on the results of its scout RC drilling programme around the margins of the La Colorada Lithocap at its Especularita project.

Highlights:

  • 106 metres ("m") @ 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo from surface, including;
  • 54m @ 0.54% Cu and 66ppm Mo
  • Scout RC drilling results deliver a Cu-Mo discovery and "walk up" drill target at Artemisa and vectors future exploration toward potentially larger system beneath the La Colorada advanced argillic lithocap
  • Phase I diamond drilling has commenced at Artemisa following up Hole ART26-RC009 which intersected significant Cu-Mo mineralisation from surface including1
  • Diamond drilling to provide geological control (2 holes, 500m) to the earlier scout RC results at Artemisa
  • Porphyry copper style potassic alteration also intersected at Piedras Blancas, providing a very strong eastward exploration vector towards the La Colorada lithocap
  • Gold-base metal veins intersected in RC drilling at Victoria and Artemisa South provide a strong northward exploration vector for potential porphyry copper mineralisation beneath the La Colorada lithocap
  • Compilation of lithocap data is in progress to guide first pass scout drilling through the La Colorada lithocap to target large-scale porphyry copper systems
  • GSC holds rights to own 100% of the Especularita project, including the Artemisa and lithocap prospects
  • Prospect located at low elevation with excellent access to infrastructure and mining services and along trend of major copper deposits including Los Pelambres, Altar and El Pachon.

Sam Garrett, Chief Executive Officer of Great Southern Copper, said:"We are very excited to announce that drilling has also now commenced at Artemisa, where earlier this year the Company discovered porphyry Cu-Mo mineralisation as part of its reconnaissance RC drilling programme targeting porphyry-style alteration identified around the southwest margins of the La Colorada lithocap. This short, two-hole programme is designed to provide geological control to the RC drilling and will be followed by a more extensive RC drilling campaign.

"The discovery at Artemisa is very significant for several reasons, namely; it supports GSC's working hypothesis that the La Colorada lithocap alteration is developed above a porphyry copper mineral system, the outer extent of the lithocap alteration has been eroded, potentially exposing the upper zones of porphyry copper systems, mineralisation in hole RC009 occurs from surface and is of potential economic grade, and the prospect occurs at low altitude, near to the coast and to infrastructure and mining support services.

"Beyond the discovery in hole RC009, the overall results of the scout RC survey have been highly successful, providing very strong exploration vector information indicating that the southwest corner of the La Colorada lithocap is highly prospective for buried porphyry copper systems. Detailed mapping and data compilation of this area of the lithocap are now underway to guide the design of the first drilling programme of the lithocap itself, which we plan to commence within the next 3-6 months."

La Colorada Porphyry Lithocap, Especularita Project:

The Company's Especularita Project is centred upon the La Colorada lithocap (Figure 1), a giant high-sulphidation advanced argillic alteration system that is highly prospective for concealed porphyry copper deposits as well as other porphyry-related types of mineralisation which may occur within or marginal to the lithocap environment. These include the advanced Cerro Negro prospect, located on the eastern side of the lithocap, where in 2025 the Company discovered high-grade Cu-Ag mineralisation beneath the old Mostaza mine workings.

The Project is situated at low altitude within the Cretaceous-age coastal metallogenic belt, within a northwest-southeast trending structural lineament that links the Project with notable large-scale porphyry Cu-Au mines and projects, including Los Pelambres, Altar and El Pachon (Figure 1).

Figure 1:GSC's Especularita Project is located at low altitude within the coastal metallogenic belt of northern Chile and within 50km radius of over 50Mt of contained copper metal defined in mines and advanced projects.

Whilst the La Colorada lithocap covers a vast area (>75km2), previous work by GSC geologists has also identified porphyry-related silica-sericite-pyrite (phyllic) alteration outcropping over large areas surrounding the lithocap suggesting that the high sulphidation alteration potentially once extended further to the west and south well beyond its present limits and has since been eroded possibly exposing the upper zones of porphyry copper systems.

To evaluate this idea GSC designed a "Proof-of-Concept" reconnaissance drill programme comprising 17 scout RC holes (2,474m) testing four target areas on the western and southwestern flanks of the advanced argillic lithocap alteration including Piedras Blancas2, Artemisa North3, Victoria4and Artemisa South5(Figure 1).

The scout RC programme was completed in July 2026 and successfully demonstrated that phyllic-altered rocks mapped at the margins of the lithocap are related to porphyry alteration systems and, more significantly, that porphyry Cu-Mo mineralisation associated with potassic (biotite-magnetite) alteration was discovered at surface with hole ART26-RC009 intersecting 106m at 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo1. Whilst the hole RC009 results represent a walk-up porphyry Cu-Mo drill target, the results from RC holes at Piedras Blancas, Artemisa South and Victoria provide strong exploration vectors indicating an increase in alteration intensity toward (and beneath) the La Colorada high-sulphidation lithocap.

Diamond Drilling Commences at Artemisa Cu-Mo Prospect:

Diamond drilling has commenced at Artemisa where hole ART26-RC009 intersected over 100m of highly anomalous Cu-Mo mineralisation. A short programme of two scout diamond holes (500m) is planned to provide geological control to hole RC009 which intersected 106m of 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo from surface, including 54m of 0.46% Cu and 66ppm Mo from 16m1(Figure 2). Diamond hole ART26-DH018 is in progress behind hole RC009 and drilling at a steeper angle to provide detailed geological information including the lithologies, alteration, and mineralisation, and their spatial and temporal relationships; critical information not available from reverse circulation drilling which is essential for planning the next stage of exploration. A second hole is planned to test the vein alteration and mineralisation mapped in an orthogonal direction to the veining and fracturing intersected in holes RC009 and DH018.

Figure 2:Planned diamond drilling at Artemisa for hole ART26-DH18 (l), outcropping evidence of potential porphyry style vein alteration identified at Artemisa (r).

The diamond drilling programme will be followed by a second, more extensive phase of RC drilling (2,000m), subject to results of the scout diamond drilling.

Scout RC Drilling Programme:

At Piedras Blancas, located approx. 1.2km north of hole RC009 (Figure 3), holes RC001, RC002 and RC004 intersected andesite volcanics intruded by diorite, quartz diorite and monzodiorite. From surface, intense phyllic alteration and quartz-pyrite veinlets grade at depth into potassic alteration3dominated by secondary biotite and characteristic biotite veinlets (or EB veins). RC003 was lost at shallow depth and twinned by RC004. Anomalous assay grades of Cu, Au and Mo are consistent with a distal position in a porphyry system (Table 1). West and north of Piedras Blancas outcropping veinlet-hosted propylitic alteration with anomalous Pb and Zn indicates that the porphyry centre lies to the south (Artemisa North) and or to the east (La Colorada). At present, Piedras Blancas is interpreted to represent the distal top of a porphyry copper system at the transition from phyllic to potassic alteration zones on the edge of the now eroded lithocap. Importantly, this drilling suggests that the base of the lithocap and top of the porphyry copper environment has been identified shallower than expected which has significant implications for drilling below the La Colorada high sulphidation lithocap alteration.

Drilling at Artemisa North targeted a cluster of artisanal workings located west of the La Colorada lithocap and in close juxtaposition to unaltered granodiorite of the Quilitapia Batholith (Figure 3). At surface the alteration is associated with distinctive black manganese-copper stained phyllic alteration. Holes RC005 - RC007 were drilled to the north of hole 009, along the strike of NS trending mine workings. Hole RC008 was drilled further east towards the lithocap. All holes intersected secondary biotite-magnetite alteration (potassic) overprinted by local chlorite-sericite alteration and narrow zones of disseminated and veinlet pyrite-chalcopyrite mineralisation (Table 1). Hole RC009 intersected significant Cu-Mo mineralisation (Table 1) associated with a distinctive low hill of phyllic-altered intrusives with shallow artisanal workings (Figure 2). The mineralisation and alteration remain open to the east and northeast towards the La Colorada lithocap, and to the north where it is interpreted to merge with the Piedras Blancas alteration zone (Figure 3).

Scout holes RC011 - 014 tested the Victoria target1,4(Figure 3) and intersected microdioritic intrusives overprinted by strong biotite-magnetite alteration. The potassic alteration is cut by structurally-controlled, metric wide zones of quartz-carbonate-hematite vein breccia hosting anomalous pyrite, chalcopyrite and bornite mineralisation with minor Ag, Pb, Zn and Ba (Table 1). Previous reported talus and soil sampling6,7suggest that the quantity, thickness and grade of the veins increases towards the north towards the La Colorada lithocap. Hematite and or magnetite mineralisation and green-grey chlorite-sericite alteration is not uncommon in diorite-related porphyry copper systems, and we interpret that these vein-breccias are distal to, and have their fluid source from the north below the La Colorada lithocap.

At Artemisa South scout holes RC015, RC016 and RC017 (Figure 3) tested below a swarm of NNE trending artisanal mines with Cu oxides and quartz-specular hematite vein-breccias with green-grey chlorite-sericite alteration haloes hosted in fresh granodiorite of the Quilitapia Batholith. The vein-breccias are similar those seen at Victoria but with less Fe oxides, perhaps reflecting the Fe-poor host rocks. Only rare narrow intervals of mineralisation averaging 2m of about 0.1 % Cu were intercepted (Table 1). In general, the quantity and thickness of the mineralised structures seems to increase north towards the La Colorada lithocap, which is interpreted to be the source of the mineralising fluids.

Figure 3:Geology and summary drill hole plan map for the scout RC programme, Especularita Project (left). Photograph (right) shows the mineralised microdiorite at Artemisa North in the foreground with black oxide copper staining and hills of the advanced argillic altered La Colorada lithocap in the background.

Next Steps:

The RC drilling results provide strong alteration vectors toward the southwestern portion of the lithocap being a significant exploration target for porphyry copper mineralisation. Detailed mapping of this area of the lithocap is in progress (Figure 4) which, combined with analysis of gridded soil geochemistry and ASD mineral spectroscopy, is designed to provide alteration temperature and pH maps of the lithocap vectoring drilling programmes to target the hot, acid areas of the lithocap which potentially sit above the porphyry copper systems below. First drilling beneath the lithocap is planned for the next 3-6 months.

Diamond drilling at Artemisa is currently in progress to provide geological control to the Cu-Mo assay results received in hole ART26-RC009 which were consistent with porphyry Cu-Mo type mineralisation. Subject to the results of the diamond drilling an extensive follow-up RC drilling campaign is planned to drill out the near-surface extent of Cu-Mo mineralisation at Artemisa.

Figure 4:Detailed mapping of the southwest quadrant of the lithocap has identified features consistent with the upper high sulphidation zone of a porphyry copper system including, from left to right; limonite stockwork and disseminations after leached pyrite; translucent porphyry-epithermal quartz vein; breccia pipes with limonite and lesser quartz matrix.

RC Drill Sampling Procedure:

A first-pass "Proof-of-Concept" test comprising 17 holes and 2,474m of RC drilling was completed across 4 prospects surrounding the western and southern margins of the la Colorada lithocap, namely Piedras Blancas, Artemisa North, Artemisa South and Victoria.

The RC drilling method employed at Especularita collected samples on two-metre intervals. Representative samples for each sample of the cuttings are collected in large, individually numbered plastic bags, which are then weighed and transferred to a riffle splitter where they are separated (or split), and homogenised, three times into two duplicate samples of approximately 5kg each. GSC personnel then ticket and label one of the ±5kg samples using preprinted ticket books.

Finally, standard reference materials ("SRM's" or "Standards"), blanks, and duplicate samples are inserted into the sample sequence for the purpose of quality assurance / quality control ("QAQC"). The second ±5kg sample is used for geological description and stored on site for reference. An additional "hand-specimen" reference selection of cuttings for each two-metre sample is also retained in labelled boxes as a record of the geology of the drill hole.

At the completion of each hole, the representative 5kg samples are transported as a batch from the field and delivered by Company employees to ALS Laboratories in Santago or La Serena where they are prepared for analysis (weighed, dried, crushed and pulverised). A subsequent 200g split of each sample pulp is then forwarded to the ALS geochemical laboratory in Lima, Peru, where samples are assayed for gold (30g fire assay with ICP-AES finish, ALS code AU-ICP21) and 48 major, base and trace elements by ICP-MS following a four-acid digest (ALS code ME-MS61).

RC drilling was selected for this initial proof-of-concept stage as it is faster and cheaper than diamond drilling and allows for the rapid testing of more targets for the same cost.

Notes for Editors:

About Great Southern Copper

Great Southern Copper PLC is a UK-listed mineral exploration company focused on the discovery of copper-gold-silver deposits in Chile. The Company has the option to acquire mining rights to 100% of Especularita project in the under-explored coastal belt of Chile that is prospective for large scale copper-gold-silver deposits. Chile is a globally significant mining jurisdiction being the world's largest producer and exporter of copper.

The Especularita Project is located in the coastal metallogenic belt of Chile which hosts significant copper mines and deposits, including Teck's Carmen de Andacollo copper mine, and boasts excellent access to infrastructure such as roads, power and ports. Significant historical small-scale and artisanal workings for both copper and gold are readily evident in the exploration project area. The coastal belt offers deposit type optionality for copper including porphyry and IOCG style deposits as well as newly recognised intrusive-related copper and gold deposits.

Great Southern Copper is strategically positioned to support the global market for copper – a critical battery metal in the clean energy transition around the world. The Company is actively engaged in exploration and evaluation work programmes targeting both large tonnage, low to medium grade Cu-Au as well as high-grade Cu-Ag-Au deposits.

THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION AS STIPULATED UNDER THE UK VERSION OF THE MARKET ABUSE REGULATION NO 596/2014 WHICH IS PART OF ENGLISH LAW BY VIRTUE OF THE EUROPEAN (WITHDRAWAL) ACT 2018, AS AMENDED.ON PUBLICATION OF THIS ANNOUNCEMENT VIA A REGULATORY INFORMATION SERVICE, THIS INFORMATION IS CONSIDERED TO BE IN THE PUBLIC DOMAIN.

09 November 2026

Great Southern Copper plc

("GSC" or the "Company")

Diamond Drilling Commences at Artemisa Cu-Mo Prospect

Scout RC Drilling Results Vector Porphyry Cu Exploration to La Colorada Lithocap, Especularita

Great Southern Copper plc (LSE: GSCU), the company focused on copper-gold-silver exploration in Chile, is pleased to announce the start of drilling targeting Cu-Mo mineralisation discovered in Reverse Circulation ("RC") drilling at the Artemisa prospect, plus provide an update on the results of its scout RC drilling programme around the margins of the La Colorada Lithocap at its Especularita project.

Highlights:

• 106 metres ("m") @ 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo from surface, including;
• 54m @ 0.54% Cu and 66ppm Mo
• Scout RC drilling results deliver a Cu-Mo discovery and "walk up" drill target at Artemisa and vectors future exploration toward potentially larger system beneath the La Colorada advanced argillic lithocap
• Phase I diamond drilling has commenced at Artemisa following up Hole ART26-RC009 which intersected significant Cu-Mo mineralisation from surface including1
• Diamond drilling to provide geological control (2 holes, 500m) to the earlier scout RC results at Artemisa
• Porphyry copper style potassic alteration also intersected at Piedras Blancas, providing a very strong eastward exploration vector towards the La Colorada lithocap
• Gold-base metal veins intersected in RC drilling at Victoria and Artemisa South provide a strong northward exploration vector for potential porphyry copper mineralisation beneath the La Colorada lithocap
• Compilation of lithocap data is in progress to guide first pass scout drilling through the La Colorada lithocap to target large-scale porphyry copper systems
• GSC holds rights to own 100% of the Especularita project, including the Artemisa and lithocap prospects
• Prospect located at low elevation with excellent access to infrastructure and mining services and along trend of major copper deposits including Los Pelambres, Altar and El Pachon.

Sam Garrett, Chief Executive Officer of Great Southern Copper, said:"We are very excited to announce that drilling has also now commenced at Artemisa, where earlier this year the Company discovered porphyry Cu-Mo mineralisation as part of its reconnaissance RC drilling programme targeting porphyry-style alteration identified around the southwest margins of the La Colorada lithocap. This short, two-hole programme is designed to provide geological control to the RC drilling and will be followed by a more extensive RC drilling campaign.

"The discovery at Artemisa is very significant for several reasons, namely; it supports GSC's working hypothesis that the La Colorada lithocap alteration is developed above a porphyry copper mineral system, the outer extent of the lithocap alteration has been eroded, potentially exposing the upper zones of porphyry copper systems, mineralisation in hole RC009 occurs from surface and is of potential economic grade, and the prospect occurs at low altitude, near to the coast and to infrastructure and mining support services.

"Beyond the discovery in hole RC009, the overall results of the scout RC survey have been highly successful, providing very strong exploration vector information indicating that the southwest corner of the La Colorada lithocap is highly prospective for buried porphyry copper systems. Detailed mapping and data compilation of this area of the lithocap are now underway to guide the design of the first drilling programme of the lithocap itself, which we plan to commence within the next 3-6 months."

La Colorada Porphyry Lithocap, Especularita Project:

The Company's Especularita Project is centred upon the La Colorada lithocap (Figure 1), a giant high-sulphidation advanced argillic alteration system that is highly prospective for concealed porphyry copper deposits as well as other porphyry-related types of mineralisation which may occur within or marginal to the lithocap environment. These include the advanced Cerro Negro prospect, located on the eastern side of the lithocap, where in 2025 the Company discovered high-grade Cu-Ag mineralisation beneath the old Mostaza mine workings.

The Project is situated at low altitude within the Cretaceous-age coastal metallogenic belt, within a northwest-southeast trending structural lineament that links the Project with notable large-scale porphyry Cu-Au mines and projects, including Los Pelambres, Altar and El Pachon (Figure 1).

Figure 1:GSC's Especularita Project is located at low altitude within the coastal metallogenic belt of northern Chile and within 50km radius of over 50Mt of contained copper metal defined in mines and advanced projects.

Whilst the La Colorada lithocap covers a vast area (>75km2), previous work by GSC geologists has also identified porphyry-related silica-sericite-pyrite (phyllic) alteration outcropping over large areas surrounding the lithocap suggesting that the high sulphidation alteration potentially once extended further to the west and south well beyond its present limits and has since been eroded possibly exposing the upper zones of porphyry copper systems.

To evaluate this idea GSC designed a "Proof-of-Concept" reconnaissance drill programme comprising 17 scout RC holes (2,474m) testing four target areas on the western and southwestern flanks of the advanced argillic lithocap alteration including Piedras Blancas2, Artemisa North3, Victoria4and Artemisa South5(Figure 1).

The scout RC programme was completed in July 2026 and successfully demonstrated that phyllic-altered rocks mapped at the margins of the lithocap are related to porphyry alteration systems and, more significantly, that porphyry Cu-Mo mineralisation associated with potassic (biotite-magnetite) alteration was discovered at surface with hole ART26-RC009 intersecting 106m at 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo1. Whilst the hole RC009 results represent a walk-up porphyry Cu-Mo drill target, the results from RC holes at Piedras Blancas, Artemisa South and Victoria provide strong exploration vectors indicating an increase in alteration intensity toward (and beneath) the La Colorada high-sulphidation lithocap.

Diamond Drilling Commences at Artemisa Cu-Mo Prospect:

Diamond drilling has commenced at Artemisa where hole ART26-RC009 intersected over 100m of highly anomalous Cu-Mo mineralisation. A short programme of two scout diamond holes (500m) is planned to provide geological control to hole RC009 which intersected 106m of 0.33% Cu and 42ppm Mo from surface, including 54m of 0.46% Cu and 66ppm Mo from 16m1(Figure 2). Diamond hole ART26-DH018 is in progress behind hole RC009 and drilling at a steeper angle to provide detailed geological information including the lithologies, alteration, and mineralisation, and their spatial and temporal relationships; critical information not available from reverse circulation drilling which is essential for planning the next stage of exploration. A second hole is planned to test the vein alteration and mineralisation mapped in an orthogonal direction to the veining and fracturing intersected in holes RC009 and DH018.

Figure 2:Planned diamond drilling at Artemisa for hole ART26-DH18 (l), outcropping evidence of potential porphyry style vein alteration identified at Artemisa (r).

The diamond drilling programme will be followed by a second, more extensive phase of RC drilling (2,000m), subject to results of the scout diamond drilling.

Scout RC Drilling Programme:

At Piedras Blancas, located approx. 1.2km north of hole RC009 (Figure 3), holes RC001, RC002 and RC004 intersected andesite volcanics intruded by diorite, quartz diorite and monzodiorite. From surface, intense phyllic alteration and quartz-pyrite veinlets grade at depth into potassic alteration3dominated by secondary biotite and characteristic biotite veinlets (or EB veins). RC003 was lost at shallow depth and twinned by RC004. Anomalous assay grades of Cu, Au and Mo are consistent with a distal position in a porphyry system (Table 1). West and north of Piedras Blancas outcropping veinlet-hosted propylitic alteration with anomalous Pb and Zn indicates that the porphyry centre lies to the south (Artemisa North) and or to the east (La Colorada). At present, Piedras Blancas is interpreted to represent the distal top of a porphyry copper system at the transition from phyllic to potassic alteration zones on the edge of the now eroded lithocap. Importantly, this drilling suggests that the base of the lithocap and top of the porphyry copper environment has been identified shallower than expected which has significant implications for drilling below the La Colorada high sulphidation lithocap alteration.

Drilling at Artemisa North targeted a cluster of artisanal workings located west of the La Colorada lithocap and in close juxtaposition to unaltered granodiorite of the Quilitapia Batholith (Figure 3). At surface the alteration is associated with distinctive black manganese-copper stained phyllic alteration. Holes RC005 - RC007 were drilled to the north of hole 009, along the strike of NS trending mine workings. Hole RC008 was drilled further east towards the lithocap. All holes intersected secondary biotite-magnetite alteration (potassic) overprinted by local chlorite-sericite alteration and narrow zones of disseminated and veinlet pyrite-chalcopyrite mineralisation (Table 1). Hole RC009 intersected significant Cu-Mo mineralisation (Table 1) associated with a distinctive low hill of phyllic-altered intrusives with shallow artisanal workings (Figure 2). The mineralisation and alteration remain open to the east and northeast towards the La Colorada lithocap, and to the north where it is interpreted to merge with the Piedras Blancas alteration zone (Figure 3).

Scout holes RC011 - 014 tested the Victoria target1,4(Figure 3) and intersected microdioritic intrusives overprinted by strong biotite-magnetite alteration. The potassic alteration is cut by structurally-controlled, metric wide zones of quartz-carbonate-hematite vein breccia hosting anomalous pyrite, chalcopyrite and bornite mineralisation with minor Ag, Pb, Zn and Ba (Table 1). Previous reported talus and soil sampling6,7suggest that the quantity, thickness and grade of the veins increases towards the north towards the La Colorada lithocap. Hematite and or magnetite mineralisation and green-grey chlorite-sericite alteration is not uncommon in diorite-related porphyry copper systems, and we interpret that these vein-breccias are distal to, and have their fluid source from the north below the La Colorada lithocap.

At Artemisa South scout holes RC015, RC016 and RC017 (Figure 3) tested below a swarm of NNE trending artisanal mines with Cu oxides and quartz-specular hematite vein-breccias with green-grey chlorite-sericite alteration haloes hosted in fresh granodiorite of the Quilitapia Batholith. The vein-breccias are similar those seen at Victoria but with less Fe oxides, perhaps reflecting the Fe-poor host rocks. Only rare narrow intervals of mineralisation averaging 2m of about 0.1 % Cu were intercepted (Table 1). In general, the quantity and thickness of the mineralised structures seems to increase north towards the La Colorada lithocap, which is interpreted to be the source of the mineralising fluids.

Figure 3:Geology and summary drill hole plan map for the scout RC programme, Especularita Project (left). Photograph (right) shows the mineralised microdiorite at Artemisa North in the foreground with black oxide copper staining and hills of the advanced argillic altered La Colorada lithocap in the background.

Next Steps:

The RC drilling results provide strong alteration vectors toward the southwestern portion of the lithocap being a significant exploration target for porphyry copper mineralisation. Detailed mapping of this area of the lithocap is in progress (Figure 4) which, combined with analysis of gridded soil geochemistry and ASD mineral spectroscopy, is designed to provide alteration temperature and pH maps of the lithocap vectoring drilling programmes to target the hot, acid areas of the lithocap which potentially sit above the porphyry copper systems below. First drilling beneath the lithocap is planned for the next 3-6 months.

Diamond drilling at Artemisa is currently in progress to provide geological control to the Cu-Mo assay results received in hole ART26-RC009 which were consistent with porphyry Cu-Mo type mineralisation. Subject to the results of the diamond drilling an extensive follow-up RC drilling campaign is planned to drill out the near-surface extent of Cu-Mo mineralisation at Artemisa.

Figure 4:Detailed mapping of the southwest quadrant of the lithocap has identified features consistent with the upper high sulphidation zone of a porphyry copper system including, from left to right; limonite stockwork and disseminations after leached pyrite; translucent porphyry-epithermal quartz vein; breccia pipes with limonite and lesser quartz matrix.

RC Drill Sampling Procedure:

A first-pass "Proof-of-Concept" test comprising 17 holes and 2,474m of RC drilling was completed across 4 prospects surrounding the western and southern margins of the la Colorada lithocap, namely Piedras Blancas, Artemisa North, Artemisa South and Victoria.

The RC drilling method employed at Especularita collected samples on two-metre intervals. Representative samples for each sample of the cuttings are collected in large, individually numbered plastic bags, which are then weighed and transferred to a riffle splitter where they are separated (or split), and homogenised, three times into two duplicate samples of approximately 5kg each. GSC personnel then ticket and label one of the ±5kg samples using preprinted ticket books.

Finally, standard reference materials ("SRM's" or "Standards"), blanks, and duplicate samples are inserted into the sample sequence for the purpose of quality assurance / quality control ("QAQC"). The second ±5kg sample is used for geological description and stored on site for reference. An additional "hand-specimen" reference selection of cuttings for each two-metre sample is also retained in labelled boxes as a record of the geology of the drill hole.

At the completion of each hole, the representative 5kg samples are transported as a batch from the field and delivered by Company employees to ALS Laboratories in Santago or La Serena where they are prepared for analysis (weighed, dried, crushed and pulverised). A subsequent 200g split of each sample pulp is then forwarded to the ALS geochemical laboratory in Lima, Peru, where samples are assayed for gold (30g fire assay with ICP-AES finish, ALS code AU-ICP21) and 48 major, base and trace elements by ICP-MS following a four-acid digest (ALS code ME-MS61).

RC drilling was selected for this initial proof-of-concept stage as it is faster and cheaper than diamond drilling and allows for the rapid testing of more targets for the same cost.

Por Heekyong Yang, Kyu-seok Shim y Tom Westbrook

SEÚL/SÍDNEY, 9 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O caían el lunes en las plataformas electrónicas, después de que una investigación interna sobre si su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera cuestionara su futuro en el fabricante de chips para IA.

La investigación interna se abrió tras una información periodística según la cual Huang había mantenido una estrecha relación con una empresaria china que presuntamente transmitía información a Pekín. Huang dijo a los empleados de Nvidia que había sido infiel a su esposa, sin revelar detalles de la relación.

La investigación, anunciada el domingo, ha centrado la atención en el futuro de Huang, dada la condición de Nvidia como el fabricante de chips de mayor valor bursátil del mundo y el papel de su director ejecutivo como el vendedor más prolífico del auge de la IA.

Las repercusiones se extendieron a Corea del Sur, donde Madison Huang, hija de Huang y ejecutiva de Nvidia, canceló una visita prevista a Seúl para asistir a una conferencia de la compañía que debía comenzar el lunes, según las empresas con las que tenía programado reunirse.

Las cotizaciones de los futuros perpetuos en la plataforma Hyperliquid y de las acciones negociadas fuera del horario habitual en el sistema Blue Ocean situaban los títulos de Nvidia en torno a los 180,30 dólares por acción, alrededor de un 3,4% por debajo del precio de cierre del viernes en el Nasdaq, de 186,64 dólares.

"Probablemente, el mercado te está diciendo ahora que esto no favorece en absoluto a la acción en un momento en que hay muchas conjeturas sobre la expansión de los centros de datos", dijo Chris Weston, director de análisis de la firma de corretaje Pepperstone, en Melbourne.

Sin embargo, Weston dijo que no creía que Huang, a quien describió como el "padrino de la IA", fuera a ser reemplazado.

"Si realmente pensáramos que va a dimitir, (...) la acción se desplomaría; sería una auténtica sangría, para ser sincero", afirmó.

The New York Times informó el mes pasado de que Jensen Huang había mantenido una relación con Alice Huang, una exdirectiva de la empresa Megaspeed, con sede en Singapur, con quien no tiene parentesco. Las autoridades estadounidenses la investigaron y concluyeron que era una colaboradora de los servicios de inteligencia chinos.

Megaspeed no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios el lunes, día festivo en Singapur.

Alice Huang no respondió a The New York Times el mes pasado, cuando el diario informó por primera vez de su relación con Huang, y Reuters no pudo localizarla para solicitarle comentarios el lunes.

SOCIOS ASIÁTICOS SIN REPERCUSIONES

Las acciones de los principales proveedores asiáticos de chips de Nvidia, TSMC 2330.TW, Samsung Electronics 005930.KS y SK Hynix 000660.KS, rebotaban el lunes tras las ventas masivas de títulos vinculados a la IA de la semana pasada. Las acciones de TSMC subían un 6,5%, mientras que las de Samsung y SK Hynix avanzaban un 2,9% y un 4,7%, respectivamente.

Algunas figuras destacadas se pronunciaron sobre la admisión de Huang. El inversor multimillonario Bill Ackman, fundador de Pershing Square Capital Management, dijo en la red social X que el director ejecutivo de Nvidia era un "ser humano increíble", pero que, si "esto realmente va más allá de una aventura, entonces es obviamente un verdadero problema".

"Espero que se trate de una simple aventura, no de un riesgo para nuestra seguridad nacional", añadió.

El director ejecutivo de Tesla, Elon Musk, dijo que estaba "de acuerdo" en una publicación del socio de Sequoia Shaun Maguire, quien afirmó que Huang "hizo algo increíblemente estúpido" que era "malo para Estados Unidos", pero que "Jensen es irremplazable para el liderazgo estadounidense en IA".

El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo que no había hablado con Huang sobre las acusaciones, pero lo calificó de buena persona. "Espero que todo esté bien. Ha hecho un trabajo increíble", añadió.

Preguntado sobre si creía que debería haber actuado cuando se le comunicaron los hallazgos de inteligencia, Trump dijo: "No, no lo creo. Creo que es un hombre honorable. Creo que probablemente tenga una explicación. Hay que escucharla".

The New York Times informó de que Trump fue informado de los hallazgos de inteligencia hace aproximadamente un año y decidió no hacer nada con esa información.

(Reporte de Kyu-seok Shim y Heekyong Yang en Seúl, Tom Westbrook en Sídney y Roger Tung en Taipéi; escrito por Brenda Goh; edición de Ed Davies y Jamie Freed; edición en español de Benjamín Mejías Valencia)
