Por Heekyong Yang, Kyu-seok Shim y Tom Westbrook

SEÚL/SÍDNEY, 9 nov (Reuters) - Las acciones de Nvidia NVDA.O caían el lunes en las plataformas electrónicas, después de que una investigación interna sobre si su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objetivo de una operación de inteligencia extranjera cuestionara su futuro en el fabricante de chips para IA.

La investigación interna se abrió tras una información periodística según la cual Huang había mantenido una estrecha relación con una empresaria china que presuntamente transmitía información a Pekín. Huang dijo a los empleados de Nvidia que había sido infiel a su esposa, sin revelar detalles de la relación.

La investigación, anunciada el domingo, ha centrado la atención en el futuro de Huang, dada la condición de Nvidia como el fabricante de chips de mayor valor bursátil del mundo y el papel de su director ejecutivo como el vendedor más prolífico del auge de la IA.

Las repercusiones se extendieron a Corea del Sur, donde Madison Huang, hija de Huang y ejecutiva de Nvidia, canceló una visita prevista a Seúl para asistir a una conferencia de la compañía que debía comenzar el lunes, según las empresas con las que tenía programado reunirse.

Las cotizaciones de los futuros perpetuos en la plataforma Hyperliquid y de las acciones negociadas fuera del horario habitual en el sistema Blue Ocean situaban los títulos de Nvidia en torno a los 180,30 dólares por acción, alrededor de un 3,4% por debajo del precio de cierre del viernes en el Nasdaq, de 186,64 dólares.

"Probablemente, el mercado te está diciendo ahora que esto no favorece en absoluto a la acción en un momento en que hay muchas conjeturas sobre la expansión de los centros de datos", dijo Chris Weston, director de análisis de la firma de corretaje Pepperstone, en Melbourne.

Sin embargo, Weston dijo que no creía que Huang, a quien describió como el "padrino de la IA", fuera a ser reemplazado.

"Si realmente pensáramos que va a dimitir, (...) la acción se desplomaría; sería una auténtica sangría, para ser sincero", afirmó.

The New York Times informó el mes pasado de que Jensen Huang había mantenido una relación con Alice Huang, una exdirectiva de la empresa Megaspeed, con sede en Singapur, con quien no tiene parentesco. Las autoridades estadounidenses la investigaron y concluyeron que era una colaboradora de los servicios de inteligencia chinos.

Megaspeed no respondió de inmediato a una solicitud de comentarios el lunes, día festivo en Singapur.

Alice Huang no respondió a The New York Times el mes pasado, cuando el diario informó por primera vez de su relación con Huang, y Reuters no pudo localizarla para solicitarle comentarios el lunes.

SOCIOS ASIÁTICOS SIN REPERCUSIONES

Las acciones de los principales proveedores asiáticos de chips de Nvidia, TSMC 2330.TW, Samsung Electronics 005930.KS y SK Hynix 000660.KS, rebotaban el lunes tras las ventas masivas de títulos vinculados a la IA de la semana pasada. Las acciones de TSMC subían un 6,5%, mientras que las de Samsung y SK Hynix avanzaban un 2,9% y un 4,7%, respectivamente.

Algunas figuras destacadas se pronunciaron sobre la admisión de Huang. El inversor multimillonario Bill Ackman, fundador de Pershing Square Capital Management, dijo en la red social X que el director ejecutivo de Nvidia era un "ser humano increíble", pero que, si "esto realmente va más allá de una aventura, entonces es obviamente un verdadero problema".

"Espero que se trate de una simple aventura, no de un riesgo para nuestra seguridad nacional", añadió.

El director ejecutivo de Tesla, Elon Musk, dijo que estaba "de acuerdo" en una publicación del socio de Sequoia Shaun Maguire, quien afirmó que Huang "hizo algo increíblemente estúpido" que era "malo para Estados Unidos", pero que "Jensen es irremplazable para el liderazgo estadounidense en IA".

El presidente de Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, dijo el domingo que no había hablado con Huang sobre las acusaciones, pero lo calificó de buena persona. "Espero que todo esté bien. Ha hecho un trabajo increíble", añadió.

Preguntado sobre si creía que debería haber actuado cuando se le comunicaron los hallazgos de inteligencia, Trump dijo: "No, no lo creo. Creo que es un hombre honorable. Creo que probablemente tenga una explicación. Hay que escucharla".

The New York Times informó de que Trump fue informado de los hallazgos de inteligencia hace aproximadamente un año y decidió no hacer nada con esa información.

(Reporte de Kyu-seok Shim y Heekyong Yang en Seúl, Tom Westbrook en Sídney y Roger Tung en Taipéi; escrito por Brenda Goh; edición de Ed Davies y Jamie Freed; edición en español de Benjamín Mejías Valencia)

(( Kyu-seok.Shim@thomsonreuters.com ))

PEKÍN, 9 nov (Reuters) - El Ministerio de Asuntos Exteriores de China, al ser preguntado el lunes sobre la investigación de Nvidia NVDA.O para determinar si su director ejecutivo, Jensen Huang, había sido objeto de una operación de inteligencia extranjera, afirmó que la «denominada narrativa del espionaje chino» carece de fundamento.

El portavoz del Ministerio, Guo Jiakun, hizo estas declaraciones en una rueda de prensa diaria celebrada en Pekín.

Peru could surpass Chile and become the fourth-largest economy in South America by 2027, according to projections from the International Monetary Fund (IMF). This information is based on the IMF's World Economic Outlook report, as cited by the Chilean newspaper La Tercera.

According to the international organization, Peru's Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is expected to reach $413.597 billion by 2027, slightly above the $413.443 billion projected for Chile. Thus, the national economy would overtake the Chilean economy in the regional ranking. The gap is expected to widen by 2028: the IMF estimates Peru's GDP will reach $435 billion, compared to Chile's $430.4 billion.

By 2031, the national economy is projected to hit $502 billion, while the Chilean economy would stand at $486.5 billion. This growth is partly attributed to higher expected growth rates for Peru. For 2026, the IMF projects a 3% expansion for the Peruvian economy, compared to an estimated 0.6% for Chile. In 2027, the rates would be 2.9% and 2.6%, respectively.

The difference is expected to remain in 2028, when Peru would grow by 3% and Chile by 2.3%. For 2031, projections indicate a 3.2% expansion for Peru and 2.4% for the Chilean economy.

In terms of size, both economies remain very close to each other. In 2025, Peru's GDP was approximately $342 billion, compared to Chile's $357.4 billion. For the year 2026, the IMF estimates Chile's economy will reach $402.2 billion, while Peru's will come in at $399.6 billion. However, La Tercera warns that Peru could surpass its neighbor even before 2027. The Chilean outlet noted that the country's economy experienced a decline of 0.4% between January and September 2026. To meet the annual growth projection of 0.6% for the entire year, Chile would need to expand by 3.6% in the last quarter.

Brazil will remain the largest economy in South America, with a projected GDP of $2.65 trillion for this year. According to the IMF, this figure would rise to $3.39 trillion by 2031. Argentina will hold second place, with an estimated GDP of $768.206 billion for this year and $855.399 billion by 2031. Colombia will retain the third position with a GDP of $572.375 billion in 2026 and a projection of $762.670 billion for 2031.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico S.A.B. de C.V. (GAP) is a prominent Mexican airport operator, managing a network of 12 airports primarily in the Pacific region, including key hubs like Guadalajara and Puerto Vallarta. Its core business centers on the operation, maintenance, and development of these facilities, encompassing passenger and cargo handling, aeronautical services, and non-aeronautical revenue streams such as retail, advertising, and parking. GAP has seen robust growth in passenger traffic, with international routes emerging as the fastest-growing segment, fueled by rising tourism and business travel demands. Additionally, cargo operations and commercial activities, particularly e-commerce-related logistics, have expanded rapidly, contributing to overall revenue diversification. This strategic focus on infrastructure upgrades and efficiency enhancements positions GAP as a key player in Mexico's aviation sector, supporting economic connectivity and sustainable growth. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Engineering & construction company by market capitalization.

SECTION 6 CORPORATE PROFILE

6.1 Activities

America Movil S.A.B. de C.V., a leading telecommunications provider headquartered in Mexico, operates across Latin America, including Mexico, Central and South America, and the Caribbean. The company specializes in mobile and fixed-line telephony, broadband internet, pay television, and related digital services, serving over 280 million customers through its extensive network infrastructure. Its core business revolves around delivering wireless communication, high-speed data connectivity, and entertainment solutions, with a strong emphasis on innovation in 5G technology and fiber-optic expansions. The fastest-growing segments include mobile data services, driven by rising smartphone adoption and demand for streaming content, as well as broadband offerings through fiber-to-the-home deployments, which have seen significant expansion in urban and emerging markets. This strategic focus has positioned America Movil as a key player in bridging the digital divide, fostering economic growth in the regions it serves. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 3rd largest Telecommunication company by market capitalization.

6.1 Activities

Fomento Económico Mexicana S.A.B. de C.V. (FEMSA), a Monterrey, Mexico-based multinational conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages through its Coca-Cola FEMSA subsidiary, which operates as one of the world's largest Coca-Cola franchisees. The company also manages a vast retail network, including the OXXO convenience store chain, which dominates Mexico's retail landscape and extends into select international markets. Additionally, FEMSA operates in logistics, fuel retailing, and health sciences. The fastest-growing segments include retail, driven by the aggressive expansion of OXXO stores and digital initiatives that enhance customer convenience, as well as beverage operations in emerging markets, fueled by rising consumer demand for non-alcoholic drinks and strategic acquisitions. This diversified approach has positioned FEMSA as a resilient player in the global consumer goods sector, emphasizing innovation and sustainability. It is the International Depository Receipt (IDR) market's 5th largest Beverages company by market capitalization.

Monterrey, Nuevo León.- FEMSA is evaluating the incorporation of robots in its OXXO stores across Mexico to check merchandise on shelves and perform some cleaning tasks. The company aims to streamline operations in its branches and mitigate the impact of labor costs on its operating expenses.

Martín Arias, FEMSA's financial director, explained during the third quarter results conference for 2026 that one of the evaluated robots could navigate the aisles and record how many products remain on the shelves. This information would assist staff in identifying shortages and restocking merchandise.

The executive also proposed using small robots to clean stores that operate 24 hours a day. These machines could handle that task for one or two hours while staff focus on other duties. Arias noted that the implementation will depend on the cost and the feasibility of the technology in Mexico.

The review of the operational model includes adjustments in shift organization and aligns with the gradual reduction of the workweek.

Starting January 1, 2027, the maximum weekly hours will decrease from 48 to 46 hours and will reduce by two hours each year until it reaches 40 hours by 2030, according to the decree published in the Federal Official Gazette.

FEMSA also anticipates pressure due to the upcoming adjustment in the minimum wage, the amount for 2027 is yet to be officially defined. Arias stated that the company pays above the minimum and expects labor expenses to represent a larger proportion of its revenues in the short term.

FEMSA has initiated a reorganization of its network of establishments in Mexico and other markets, closing OXXO stores, pharmacies, and gas stations, in stark contrast to its discount store chain, Bara, which continues to see notable growth in a market where it competes with Tiendas 3B. In its third quarter financial report for 2026, the company disclosed that it closed 140 OXXO stores in Mexico between July and September as part of a portfolio optimization program. However, during the same period, it opened 191 stores, leading to a net gain of 51 units and a total of 24,759 establishments in Mexico by the end of September.

OXXO to close nearly 250 stores between July and December FEMSA also reduces its number of pharmacies

The streamlining of OXXO establishments is part of an exercise to optimize its commercial network. Throughout the third quarter, FEMSA completed the closure of 140 units and expects to wrap up a process that will affect approximately 250 stores between July and December 2026. In the first nine months of the year, OXXO Mexico recorded a total of 272 closures and 734 openings, resulting in a net growth of 462 establishments. The process affected the financial results of the division, as the operational costs associated with the store closures impacted approximately 0.20% of OXXO Mexico's operating profit. According to the company, without this effect, the segment's operating profit would have increased by 8% in the third quarter instead of the reported 5.8%. This reorganization is not limited to convenience stores; FEMSA's Health division, which encompasses its pharmacy businesses, experienced a closure of 15 establishments during the third quarter, ending September with 4,569 units. In Mexico, the decline was more pronounced, with the company reducing its pharmacies from 1,315 in the third quarter of 2025 to 1,259 in the same period of 2026, marking an annual drop of 4.3%. However, FEMSA explained that the adjustments in its Health division also respond to changes in other markets. One major reason is the gradual exit from its institutional pharmaceutical dispensing business in Colombia, particularly following the end of its contract with EPS Sanitas. Additionally, there are commercial initiatives in Chile aimed at adjusting its network of establishments in response to an increasingly competitive environment.

OXXO Gas loses service stations OXXO's business in Europe also had to close stores as Bara grows while other FEMSA businesses reduce establishments

Another business that reduced its physical presence was the service station segment, which is part of FEMSA's Americas and Mobility division. By the end of September, the company reported 772 stations, nine fewer than in the previous quarter. Of this total, 544 are located in Mexico and 228 in the United States. The accumulated reduction was 18 net stations during the first nine months of 2026, while over the last 12 months, the contraction reached 26 units. In addition to the changes in its network, the fuel business faced profitability pressures due to rising input costs and voluntary maximum pricing commitments adopted in Mexico. This trend of adjustments has also reached Europe, where Valora, a company dedicated to convenience retailing and food, operates. In the third quarter of 2026, its network decreased from 2,772 to 2,762 establishments compared to the same period last year, a decline of 0.4%. The company attributed some of the operational difficulties in Germany to adverse weather conditions, disruptions in rail traffic, and a lower volume in its business-to-business (B2B) sales. In contrast to the adjustments recorded in OXXO, pharmacies, service stations, and Valora, Bara maintained an accelerated expansion strategy. The discount store chain added 112 net establishments during the third quarter, reaching a total of 898 units by the end of September, representing an annual growth of 56.7%.

Over the last 12 months, Bara has incorporated 325 net stores, reflecting FEMSA's commitment to strengthening this commercial format. In comparison, during the same period, Tiendas 3B opened 141 net establishments between July and September, 29 more than Bara, which added 112.

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

SECTION 1: BIOGRAPHY: RAUL REVUELTA MUSALEM, CEO

Bachelor of Economics from the Instituto Tecnologico de Estudios Superiores de Monterrey, was appointed CEO of Grupo Aeroportuario del Pacifico (GAP) in April 2018. He has 20 years of experience in the airport and infrastructure sector.

Between 2005 and 2015, he held various positions at GAP, including Director of Administration and Finance (CFO) and Chief Commercial Officer (CCO). One of his major achievements was leading the monumental project known as the "Cross Border Xpress," the only bi-national bridge in the world connecting Mexico and the United States, which has brought countless benefits to both nations.

Previously, he served as Deputy Director of Finance at the Secretaria de Comunicaciones y Transportes (SCT) for six years, where he participated in various privatization processes in the sector and gained extensive knowledge in the field of federal concessions.

He was recently appointed Vice President of the International Council of Airports for Latin America and the Caribbean (ACI-LAC) for the 2024-2025 term, an organization that operates in 41 countries and represents more than 350 air terminals in Latin America and the Caribbean.

The ex-dividend date is Tuesday, November 10th.

America Movil has increased its dividend payment by an average of 0.1% annually over the last three years. America Movil has a payout ratio of 34.1% meaning its dividend is sufficiently covered by earnings. Equities research analysts expect America Movil to earn $2.15 per share next year, which means the company should continue to be able to cover its $0.59 annual dividend with an expected future payout ratio of 27.4%.

America Movil Price Performance

AMX stock opened at $25.71 on Friday. The stock has a 50-day moving average price of $22.97 and a two-hundred day moving average price of $24.46. The company has a current ratio of 0.71, a quick ratio of 0.66 and a debt-to-equity ratio of 0.90.

Institutional Investors Weigh In On America Movil

A number of institutional investors and hedge funds have recently made changes to their positions in the stock. Lazard Asset Management LLC raised its position in America Movil by 17.8% during the first quarter. Lazard Asset Management LLC now owns 20,807,915 shares of the Wireless communications provider's stock worth $530,186,000 after acquiring an additional 3,140,360 shares in the last quarter. America Movil Company Profile

América Móvil is a telecommunications company headquartered in Mexico City. Established in 2000, it grew from the wireless operations of Telmex and has expanded across the Americas and Europe.

The company provides mobile and fixed-line voice services, broadband internet, pay television and data services to residential, business and government customers. It also offers enterprise connectivity and related technology services.

América Móvil operates under brands that include Telcel in Mexico, Claro in many Latin American markets and A1 in parts of Europe.

Brightline finally resumed its higher-speed train service between West Palm Beach and Orlando early Thursday after floodwaters in Brevard County blocked the Florida East Coast Railway corridor along the shoreline for most of the week.

"Brightline has resumed usual train service between Orlando and West Palm Beach today, while continuing the full corridor service to Miami," the company said in a news release issued shortly after sunrise.

"Rail traffic resumed normal operations once water levels had receded, necessary repair work was completed, and all tracks, signals and crossings cleared inspection by FECR," the announcement added.

Rail infrastructure teams worked closely with the FECR and Brevard County Emergency Management to restore service, which was shut down on Monday amid driving rainstorms and flooding that covered sections of track.

The railroad said it stayed in contact with affected customers about travel options during the closure.

Management advised customers to monitor GoBrightline.com, the Brightline app and social media channels for service updates.

"The safety of our guests, teammates and the communities we serve remains our highest priority," the company said in an earlier statement.

The railroad's South Florida service was unaffected; all trains serving West Palm Beach, Boca Raton, Fort Lauderdale, Aventura and Miami operated as scheduled.

The rail line is offering $39 "Smart Saver" fares between South Florida and Orlando. A 14-day advance purchase is required and customers must book by Jan. 10, 2027, for travel through Feb. 28, 2027, according to Brightline's website.

Grupo ISA won a bid to market advertising spaces at the nine airports operated by Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste ( ASUR ).

During a presentation to clients and business partners, the outdoor and transportation media company also introduced new projects, including the bidding for the Mexico-Toluca Intercity Train , known as El Insurgente, and road overpasses in Tijuana.

Grupo ISA's president, Hugo Camou, emphasized that these bids enhance the company's presence in strategic infrastructure , participating with advertising spaces in the metro systems of the country's three main cities: Mexico City, Guadalajara, and Monterrey, in addition to various airports.

Grupo ISA will modernize ASUR terminals

In his remarks, Raúl Camou, the general director of Grupo ISA, highlighted that digitalization will be one of the main drivers of the company's growth, through the development of innovative and technological advertising solutions.

Additionally, Claudio Góngora, ASUR's legal director, recognized Grupo ISA as a strategic partner to contribute to the modernization and enhancement of the Cancun International Airport and other terminals in the group, through a multi-year contract.

Photo credit: Cristian Laris

Grupo ISA will invest 110 million pesos

As part of this new expansion phase, the company plans to make a 110 million pesos investment in southeastern Mexico , stated Jorge García, the commercial director of Grupo ISA.

With these awards, Grupo ISA aims to strengthen its positioning in the outdoor advertising market and expand its presence in high-traffic user areas, with a strategy focused on investment and digital transformation.

Press Release article 3 of 3, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V.(NYSE: ASR; BMV: ASUR) (ASUR), a leading international airport group with operations in Mexico, the United States, and Colombia, today announced the call to assembly for its General Ordinary Shareholders' Meeting which will be held on January 26 th, 2026 and announced the agenda for the meeting. The following is the complete text of the call to assembly for the shareholders' meeting: CALL TO ASSEMBLY FOR ORDINARY ANNUAL GENERAL MEETING OF THE SHAREHOLDERS OF GRUPO AEROPORTUARIO DEL SURESTE, S.A.B. (the "Company") and Articles 181 and 183 of the General Corporations Law ("Ley General de Sociedades Mercantiles"), the Company's shareholders are hereby called to attend the Ordinary General Shareholders' Meeting (the "Meeting"), which will take place at 10 o'clock a.m. on the 26 th of January 2026, at the Company's offices at Bosque de Alisos No. 47-A 4 th floor, Colonia Bosque de las Lomas, 05120, Mexico City, Mexico, in order to discuss the following matters: A G E N D A I. Press Release article 3 of 3, Source: WEC, 313 words

Nov 18, 2025: ASUR SIGNS DEAL TO ACQUIRE MOTIVA'S STAKE IN AIRPORT BUSINESS IN BRAZIL, ECUADOR, COSTA RICA AND CURACAO

Grupo Aeroportuario del Sureste, S.A.B. de C.V. (NYSE:ASR; BMV:ASUR) ("ASUR") and Motiva Infraestrutura de Mobilidade S.A. (B3: MOTV3) ("Motiva") today announced that ASUR has entered into a purchase agreement with Motiva to acquire all of the issued and outstanding equity interest of Companhia de Participacoes em Concessoes ("CPC"), a wholly owned subsidiary of Motiva, for a purchase price of R$5,000 million (US$936 million)1,2, with an implied enterprise value R$13,700 million (US$2,566 million) 2,3. CPC owns equity interests in 20 airports with concessions in Brazil, Ecuador, Costa Rica and Curacao. The portfolio includes the Quito International Airport in Quito, Ecuador, the Juan Santamaria International Airport in San Jose, Costa Rica, the Curacao International Airport in Curacao, the Confins International Airport in Brazil, as well as the Pampulha airport, the Bloco Sul airports, and the Bloco Central airports in Brazil. The portfolio reported EBITDA for the twelve- month period ending September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$2,000 million (US$375 million 2 ) and, on a proportionate basis to CPC's stake, of R$1,300 million (US$243 million 2 ); and, net financial debt as of September 30, 2025, on an 100% basis, of R$6,300 million (US$1,180 million 2 ). The acquisition represents a stepping stone in ASUR's expansion strategy in the region adding 4 new markets in Latin America and the Caribbean, including Latin America's largest aviation market by passengers, Brazil, to ASUR's existing presence in Mexico, Colombia and Puerto Rico. This acquisition will add more than 45 million passengers to ASUR's 71 million reported in 2024, consolidating ASUR as the leading airport operator in the Americas. Out of the 20 airports in CPC's portfolio, 17 have more than 15 years remaining in their concession life.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 09, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA: A Hidden Gem in Consumer Staples

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. (KOF) is emerging as a potentially undervalued opportunity in the consumer staples sector. As of 9th July 2026, the company stands as the largest Coca-Cola bottler worldwide by sales volume, serving over 270 million consumers throughout Latin America with a diverse product range that includes sparkling beverages, water, juices, sports drinks, and dairy products.

Despite operating in a mature and competitive consumer staples industry, Coca-Cola FEMSA's current market valuation suggests that investors may be overlooking its resilient cash flows and strong profitability. The company's extensive distribution network and established brand portfolio provide a competitive edge, enabling it to generate recurring cash flow.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's intrinsic value-to-price (IV/P) ratio stands at 1.50, indicating that the stock may be trading below conservative intrinsic value estimates. The company's recent financial metrics reveal total revenue of approximately MXN 292.5 billion, operating income of about MXN 40.4 billion, and a net income of roughly MXN 23.0 billion. The firm maintains a strong free cash flow of about MXN 24.2 billion, showcasing its capability to support dividends, investments, and strategic acquisitions.

The company's financial health is further illustrated by its balance sheet, which lists total assets at approximately MXN 314.5 billion and total liabilities at around MXN 160.5 billion, resulting in a solid shareholders' equity of about MXN 154.0 billion. Despite slight increases in leverage due to acquisitions, Coca-Cola FEMSA continues to exhibit strong cash generation, enabling it to navigate macroeconomic challenges such as currency volatility and inflation.

While market concerns such as slowing consumer spending and rising commodity costs persist, Coca-Cola FEMSA's fundamentals remain compelling. With an Acquirer's Multiple of 4.0 and robust operating margins, the company appears to be a promising long-term investment for value-seeking investors looking at the consumer staples sector.

Jul 05, 2026: Coca-Cola Femsa Expands Beverage Operations for Long-Term Growth

Coca-Cola Femsa S.A.B. de C.V., the largest Coca-Cola bottler in the world by volume, continues to leverage its wide Latin American footprint and franchise agreements to drive beverage distribution and long-term growth opportunities. As of the 5th of July, 2026, Coca-Cola Femsa's operations underline a robust business model focused on efficiency and localized strategies that resonate with regional consumer preferences.

Coca-Cola Femsa oversees a broad network of bottling plants and distribution centers that support a high-frequency, high-volume beverage business in both emerging and developed Latin American economies. Its territories include key markets such as Mexico, Brazil, and other countries in Central and South America, where population density and urbanization provide a large consumer base for ready-to-drink beverages. The company manages operations spanning manufacturing, warehousing, logistics, and last-mile delivery to retailers, restaurants, and other points of sale.

The company operates under long-term franchise and bottling agreements that define its rights and obligations to produce, market, and sell Coca-Cola branded beverages in assigned territories. Within this framework, Coca-Cola Femsa focuses on operational efficiency, portfolio management, and local commercial strategies while coordinating with the brand owner on marketing and innovation. This strategic approach allows the company to combine globally recognized brands with local knowledge of consumer preferences and retail formats.

Beyond classic colas, Coca-Cola Femsa manages a broad beverage portfolio that typically includes flavored sparkling soft drinks, still juices, sports drinks, teas, and bottled water. The company adapts flavors, package sizes, and multipack configurations to local consumer tastes and price points, ensuring a tailored approach that meets diverse market demands. Packaging innovation plays a central role in Coca-Cola Femsa's operations, as the company strives to meet sustainability expectations and improve efficiency.

From an investor perspective, Coca-Cola Femsa is often viewed as a consumer staples business with exposure to multiple Latin American currencies and macroeconomic environments. Analysts closely monitor capital expenditure commitments, leverage metrics, and dividend policies when assessing the balance between growth investment and shareholder returns. For many global investors, Coca-Cola Femsa represents an opportunity to tap into Latin American consumer trends through a well-established beverage platform tied to iconic soft drink brands.

Jun 23, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Launches 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle to Enhance Family Consumption

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. has unveiled its new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle, targeting family consumption in key Mexican markets. This launch, taking place on 23rd June 2026, is a significant step in the company's strategy to enhance the availability of reusable packaging solutions.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Grupo Aeroportuario del Centro Norte S.A.B. de C.V. (OMA), a leading airport operator in Mexico, manages a network of 13 airports primarily in the northern and central regions, including key hubs like Monterrey. Its core business revolves around aeronautical services, such as passenger and cargo handling, alongside non-aeronautical activities including retail concessions, real estate development, and commercial leasing. OMA's fastest-growing segments include international passenger traffic, driven by increasing tourism and trade links, as well as cargo operations, which have expanded with e-commerce and cross-border logistics. Additionally, the company has seen robust growth in non-aeronautical revenues from diversified sources like parking and advertising, supporting overall profitability. Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

Jul 20, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte's Growth Strategy Emphasizes Sustainability and Innovation

In an exclusive interview, Mr. Jose Luis Munoz, Executive Director of Sustainability & Investor Relations at Grupo Financiero Banorte, outlined the bank's strategic position for sustainable growth. The discussion, held on the 20th of July 2026, highlighted Banorte's financial performance amid a dynamic economic landscape and its commitment to fostering long-term sustainability.

Reflecting on Banorte's 125-year legacy, Munoz emphasized that the definition of a strong bank has evolved with changing economic and geopolitical landscapes. 'Resilience has been a hallmark of Banorte's history,' he explained, noting the bank's ability to navigate various challenges, including the rise of fintech competitors and the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic. This resilience is evident in the bank's growing loan portfolio, particularly in consumer lending, which saw an increase in mortgages, auto loans, and credit cards.

The bank's commitment to the SME sector remains a cornerstone of its strategy, with dedicated resources aimed at improving customer interaction and service. Munoz explained that Banorte's extensive branch network, particularly in economically active regions, positions it favorably to cater to the needs of SMEs. The bank's approach to 'hyper-personalisation' through advanced technology and analytics further differentiates it from competitors, allowing for tailored offerings that resonate with customer needs.

Banorte's financial health is underscored by a robust capital adequacy ratio of 20.06%, well above regulatory requirements. Munoz highlighted the importance of maintaining a safety buffer due to the bank's status as a systemic institution without foreign subsidiaries. This focus on capital preservation, coupled with disciplined risk management, has enabled Banorte to sustain its strong liquidity position and support growth initiatives.

Sustainability is woven into the fabric of Banorte's operations, with initiatives such as the commitment to plant one million trees by 2030 and participation in the Task Force on Nature-related Financial Disclosures (TNFD). Munoz noted that these efforts not only enhance the bank's sustainability practices but also help clients navigate risks associated with nature and biodiversity. As Banorte continues to expand its influence in the financial sector, its commitment to innovation, customer experience, and sustainable practices positions it as a key player in Mexico's economic development.

Jul 02, 2026: Grupo Financiero Banorte Strengthens Its Position in Mexico's Banking Sector

Grupo Financiero Banorte continues to position itself as one of Mexico's largest banks, combining a traditional branch network with digital services as it competes for retail and corporate customers in a changing rate and regulatory environment. As of 2nd July 2026, Banorte operates in an environment shaped by domestic interest rates, economic growth, and evolving regulation.

Grupo Financiero Banorte S.A.B. (ISIN MXP370641013) is one of Mexico's largest financial groups, with activities spanning commercial banking, consumer finance, asset management, insurance, and pension funds. As a major lender in the Mexican market, the group plays a central role in financing households and businesses across the country. Its nationwide branch and ATM network supports a wide retail franchise, while its corporate and government banking units provide services to larger clients and public entities.

Management attention at Banorte typically centers on maintaining a balance between growth and risk, especially in areas such as consumer credit, mortgages, and small-business lending. Asset quality indicators, such as non-performing loans and coverage ratios, are closely watched, as they show how well the bank is managing credit risk in its portfolio. Additionally, capital adequacy remains a key concern, with banks expected to hold sufficient capital buffers to absorb potential losses and comply with regulatory requirements.

Banorte has invested in digital channels to complement its traditional branch network, offering online and mobile banking for individuals and businesses. These platforms allow customers to make payments, transfer funds, and apply for products such as credit cards and personal loans without visiting a branch. The ability to migrate more activity to digital channels helps Banorte improve efficiency by reducing operating costs per customer while maintaining or even expanding its customer base.

Banorte's shares are listed in Mexico, providing investors exposure to the country's financial sector through a diversified banking and financial services group. The stock's performance over time reflects local macroeconomic conditions, interest rate trends, and the bank's own profitability and risk management decisions. For equity investors, key variables often include return on equity, cost-to-income ratios, asset growth, and dividend policy, all of which shape how the market values Banorte relative to both domestic peers and international financial groups.

The Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle is designed for households that prefer purchasing beverages in bulk while maintaining the option for return and reuse. This innovative format not only aims to reduce packaging waste but also lowers the per-liter cost for consumers, who can return the bottle to local corner stores, which have long embraced returnable formats.

Mariana Rodriguez, product manager at Coca-Cola FEMSA, noted that the bottle features a more pronounced waist and a textured grip, enhancing usability at family gatherings. The design is lighter than traditional glass returnable bottles, making it easier for all family members, including children and seniors, to handle. While glass maintains a nostalgic appeal, the PET format provides a modern balance of convenience and tradition.

Coca-Cola FEMSA's CEO, John Santa Maria, has emphasized the importance of refillable packaging as a core strategy. The new 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle aligns with the company's sustainability goals, as using refillable containers can significantly reduce the carbon footprint associated with beverage consumption. This initiative not only supports environmental efforts but also fosters a culture of reuse among consumers.

Initially available in select Mexican markets, the Coca-Cola FEMSA 2.5L Returnable PET Bottle leverages the existing popularity of refillable formats. The pricing structure typically includes a deposit for the bottle, making it economically advantageous for families who purchase large quantities. This strategic move is expected to positively impact Coca-Cola FEMSA's long-term cash flow and shareholder value, as the company continues to adapt to consumer preferences while committing to sustainable practices.

Jun 17, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA Leverages Logistics-as-a-Service to Enhance Distribution

Coca-Cola FEMSA, S.A.B. de C.V. is quietly enhancing its distribution capabilities through Fomento Economico Mexicano's Logistics-as-a-Service offering. This innovative service transforms FEMSA's robust Coca-Cola delivery network into a third-party logistics solution for brands requiring efficient, temperature-controlled distribution across Mexico. This strategic move was made public on the 17th of June, 2026, and is expected to reshape the logistical landscape in the region.

FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service fundamentally allows third-party brands to access the same warehousing, routing software, and last-mile fleet utilized by Coca-Cola in Mexico and other Latin American markets. Clients can seamlessly integrate into FEMSA's extensive delivery network, which significantly reduces the need for them to establish their own complex logistics operations. This means that consumer goods can be efficiently delivered to over 3 million points of sale, utilizing existing routes that serve thousands of small retail outlets daily.

For brands, especially those in the fast-moving consumer goods sector, this service provides an invaluable shortcut to market penetration. Products delivered alongside Coca-Cola benefit from the established distribution patterns that store owners are accustomed to, thus facilitating easier acceptance and integration into existing supply chains. The service's reach can substantially expedite market entry for new energy drinks or healthcare products, compressing lengthy rollout periods into mere months.

Technological infrastructure underpins this service, with advanced routing algorithms and inventory management tools ensuring efficient operations. FEMSA's Logistics-as-a-Service also offers clients features such as order tracking and delivery proof without necessitating additional investment in software. This is particularly crucial for pharmaceuticals and health products, where stringent temperature control and delivery reliability are essential.

Logistics-as-a-Service is a strategic component of FEMSA's broader vision to maximize value from its existing infrastructure. Although still a smaller segment compared to its core Coca-Cola bottling and OXXO retail operations, it represents a significant opportunity for growth. Investors should note that while immediate scale may be limited, the long-term potential for operating leverage in this logistics venture aligns with FEMSA's overarching objective of enhancing its distribution capabilities.

Jun 15, 2026: Coca-Cola FEMSA's Returnable Glass Bottle: A Timeless Choice for Latin American Consumers

Coca-Cola FEMSA's standardized returnable glass bottle remains a core workhorse in Latin America, combining refillable packaging with industrial-scale distribution. As of 15th June 2026, the bottle continues to play a vital role, particularly in Mexico and Brazil, where refillable containers are a staple of consumer habits.

The Coca-Cola returnable glass bottle is typically available in familiar single-serve formats ranging from 235 ml to 355 ml, as well as larger family sizes such as 1.0 liter and 1.25 liters. These offerings are tailored to local preferences, making them more appealing to consumers in different markets. Beyond its nostalgic appeal, the refillable glass format serves a practical purpose in Coca-Cola FEMSA's packaging mix, providing a robust container that can endure multiple wash-and-refill cycles on industrial bottling lines.

The returnable glass bottle operates on a deposit-return system, where consumers pay a deposit upon purchase and reclaim it when they return the empty bottle. This model encourages recycling and reinforces Coca-Cola FEMSA's commitment to sustainability. In the markets where Coca-Cola FEMSA operates, these bottles are commonly found in traditional trade outlets, including neighborhood stores, small groceries, and food-service channels, coexisting alongside one-way PET bottles and cans.

For Coca-Cola FEMSA, the returnable glass bottle is not merely a product but a strategic asset that caters to price-sensitive consumers while enhancing the company's sustainability narrative around refillable packaging. The combination of tradition and practicality ensures that Coca-Cola FEMSA's returnable glass bottle remains a relevant and cherished choice.

5.1 Activities

Arca Continental SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican conglomerate, is primarily engaged in the production, bottling, and distribution of beverages as a key franchise partner for The Coca-Cola Company. The company operates across Mexico, the United States, and South America, offering a diverse portfolio that includes carbonated soft drinks, bottled water, juices, teas, and snacks. Its core activities encompass manufacturing, logistics, and sales through an extensive network of distribution channels, serving both retail and hospitality sectors. In recent years, the fastest-growing segments have been healthier beverage options, such as flavored waters and ready-to-drink teas, driven by shifting consumer preferences toward wellness and hydration products. Additionally, international expansion into markets like Ecuador and Peru has fueled growth, enhancing revenue streams and market share. Industrias Penoles SAB de CV, a prominent Mexican mining company, focuses on the exploration, extraction, and processing of metallic minerals. Among its fastest-growing segments are silver mining and precious metals processing, fueled by rising global demand in electronics, renewable energy, and industrial applications.
